# Bedrock Voice Chat — complete documentation

Proximity voice chat for Minecraft Bedrock and Java. Self-hosted: each server is
run by the community that owns it.

Individual pages: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/llms.txt

---

# Downloads

> Every BVC download — client apps, the server, Addons, and companion tools.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/start/downloads

## Client app

The Bedrock Voice Chat app lets you talk to other players in Minecraft Bedrock and Java Edition. It uses your microphone and speakers.

| Platform | Where |
|---|---|
| **Windows** | [Microsoft Store](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9npxjk015fvt?hl=en-US&gl=US), or [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Alaydriem/bedrock-voice-chat/releases). |
| **Linux** | `.deb` and AppImage on [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Alaydriem/bedrock-voice-chat/releases). |
| **macOS** | [TestFlight](https://testflight.apple.com/join/JSG7bVqC). One build is for macOS and iOS. |
| **iOS / iPadOS** | [TestFlight](https://testflight.apple.com/join/JSG7bVqC). |
| **Android** | [Google Play Beta](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.alaydriem.bvc.client). |

:::tip
Console players on Xbox, PlayStation and Switch use the mobile app on a phone or tablet. The phone or tablet is the microphone and speaker. See [console and mobile](/wiki/platforms/console-and-mobile/).

There is no Bedrock Voice Chat app for consoles. To help fund a console app, support Bedrock Voice Chat on Patreon or as a YouTube member.
:::

## Server

| Download | Where |
|---|---|
| BVC server | [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Alaydriem/bedrock-voice-chat/releases) |
| Container image | `ghcr.io/alaydriem/bedrock-voice-chat/server` |

See [Installing the BVC server](/wiki/server/installation/).

| Type | Where |
|---|---|
| Bedrock Addon | For Bedrock Dedicated Server. [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Alaydriem/bedrock-voice-chat/releases) (releases with a tag that starts with `mods-`) or [CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft-bedrock/addons/bedrock-voice-chat). |
| Realms / no-net Addon | For Realms, Aternos and other hosts that do not allow the `@minecraft/server-net` module. [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Alaydriem/bedrock-voice-chat/releases) (releases with a tag that starts with `mods-`) or [CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft-bedrock/addons/bedrock-voice-chat-for-realms). |
| Fabric and PaperMC | [Modrinth](https://modrinth.com/mod/bedrock-voice-chat). |

:::tip
To find the Addon that your host needs, see [Where BVC works](/wiki/platforms/).
:::

## Companion apps

| App | Where |
|---|---|
| Stream Deck plugin | [Elgato Marketplace](https://marketplace.elgato.com/product/bedrock-voice-chat-c5a151d6-3669-487f-9548-bfe689e50203) |

# FAQ

> Short answers to the questions that come up most.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/start/faq

## Does it work on Realms?

Yes. The BVC app connects to the Realm for you, with a feature called Bedrock Voice Chat Connect. After each Minecraft update, BVC can stop working on Realms until a matching BVC version is available. See [Realms](/wiki/platforms/realms/).

## Does it work on Aternos?

Yes. The BVC app connects to the Aternos server for you, with Bedrock Voice Chat Connect. After each Minecraft update, BVC can stop working on Aternos until a matching BVC version is available. See [Aternos](/wiki/platforms/aternos/).

## Does it work on a LAN or single-player world?

No. Bedrock Voice Chat does not work on LAN worlds or single-player worlds. Use a Realm, an Aternos server or a Bedrock Dedicated Server. See [LAN and local worlds](/wiki/platforms/lan-and-local-worlds/).

## Can I use it on Xbox, PlayStation, or Switch?

Yes. Use the mobile app on a phone or tablet. There is no console app. See [Console and mobile](/wiki/platforms/console-and-mobile/).

## Does it work with Geyser?

Yes. Install the Java mod. The mod detects Floodgate automatically. See [Geyser and Floodgate](/wiki/server/java-mod/integrations/geyser-and-floodgate/).

## Does it work with Simple Voice Chat?

Yes. The BVC Java mod connects to Simple Voice Chat. Java players on Simple Voice Chat and players on the BVC app can then hear each other. See [Simple Voice Chat](/wiki/server/java-mod/integrations/simple-voice-chat/).

You do not need Simple Voice Chat. With only the [Java mod](/wiki/server/java-mod/), your Java and Bedrock players hear each other through the BVC app.

## Is there a public server I can join?

No. There is no official server and no list of servers.

If you already play on a server that you like, ask the owner to install BVC. Send them [Running a server](/wiki/server/).

## What is my server URL?

Use the address of the BVC server. Your server operator sets up the BVC server and gives you the address. See [Signing in](/wiki/player/signing-in/).

:::danger
Bedrock Voice Chat **will not work** if you enter your Aternos server address, an IP address, or your Bedrock Dedicated Server address in the server URL field. You **MUST** use the address of the **Bedrock Voice Chat server**.
:::

## Do I need the BVC server if I use the Java mod?

Not always. The Java mod can run the BVC server inside your Minecraft server. Use this on small servers that are always on. Do not use it on low-end hosts. See [Java mod](/wiki/server/java-mod/).

## Can I record?

Yes, on desktop. Each player records to a separate track. Mobile devices cannot record. Your server operator can turn off recording. See [Recording](/wiki/creator/recording/).

## Can I read in-game chat in the app?

Yes. The app shows the server's chat, and sends your messages into the game. See [Chat](/wiki/player/chat/).

## Is it free?

Yes. [Supporting the project](/wiki/start/supporting-bvc/) funds development. Supporters get early access to new builds. This is most useful after a Minecraft update.

## I updated Minecraft and Bedrock Voice Chat stopped working

On Realms and Aternos, Bedrock Voice Chat can stop working after a Minecraft update. Each update can change the Bedrock network protocol, and BVC must be updated to match. Mojang does not document this protocol. The BVC developers can start this work only after Mojang releases the update. See [Version support](/wiki/platforms/version-support/).

A Bedrock Dedicated Server is not affected. Use one to keep voice chat working on the day of an update.

---

# Reporting an issue

> Where to report a bug or ask a question, and what to include.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/start/report-an-issue

For help, join our **[Discord](https://discord.gg/CdtchD5zxr)**.

:::tip[Check the troubleshooting page first]
The troubleshooting pages have fixes for the most common problems.

[Players](/wiki/player/troubleshooting/) · [Operators](/wiki/server/troubleshooting/)
:::

## What to include

**If you are a player:**

- Your platform: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android or iOS. If you play on a console, give the console and the phone or tablet that runs the app.
- The error code, if the app showed one.
- The server that you play on, and if other players on that server can use voice chat.
- The fixes that you already tried.

**If you run a server:**

- The output of `curl https://<your-server>/api/config`.
- If the UDP voice port is open, as well as TCP/443. A closed UDP port is the most common cause of missing audio.
- If `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://<your-server>/api/position` returns data. `<token>` is the value of `server.minecraft.access_token`.
- How you run the BVC server: Docker, directly on the host, or inside the Java mod.

**If the app crashed:** tell us what you were doing, and if the crash happens again. Attach the log file if you have it.

## Where to report

| Report | Where |
|---|---|
| Any question or problem | [Discord](https://discord.gg/CdtchD5zxr) |
| Confirmed bugs | [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Alaydriem/bedrock-voice-chat/issues). The maintainers usually open these from Discord reports. |
| Feature requests | Discord or GitHub Issues |
| Long technical discussion | [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/Alaydriem/bedrock-voice-chat/discussions) |

Search for your problem before you post.

## Security issues

:::danger[Do not open a public issue for a security problem]
Use GitHub's [private vulnerability reporting](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/security-advisories/guidance-on-reporting-and-writing-information-about-vulnerabilities/privately-reporting-a-security-vulnerability) under the Security tab.
:::

There is no bug bounty. We credit valid reports in `SECURITY.md`.

## Helping others

If you know the answer to a question on Discord, answer it. See [supporting BVC](/wiki/start/supporting-bvc/).

---

# Supporting BVC

> How to support development, financially or otherwise.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/start/supporting-bvc

Bedrock Voice Chat is free. If you want to support Bedrock Voice Chat, you can help pay for development, app store fees, test devices and server hosting.

## Financial support

**[Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/c/Alaydriem)** pays for development, app store fees, and new features.

**[YouTube](https://youtube.com/@alaydriem)** and **[Twitch](https://twitch.tv/alaydriem)** members get exclusive updates and previews of new features, and can follow development live.

Supporters get **early access to builds and packs**. On Realms and Aternos, supporters usually get a working build before the general release. To see how long support usually takes after a Minecraft update, see [version support](/wiki/platforms/version-support/).

Sign up with **[Nodecraft](https://nodecraft.com/r/alaydriem)** to get the best Nodecraft discount for Minecraft servers that run Bedrock Voice Chat.

## Free support

**Watch and comment on [YouTube](https://youtube.com/@alaydriem).** All major BVC announcements go there first.

**Watch, follow and subscribe to the [Twitch](https://www.twitch.tv/alaydriem) streams.** Streams are twice a week, on a regular schedule.

**Tell people about BVC, and send feedback.** We use bug reports and feature requests from GitHub and Discord to plan new work.

**Answer questions** on [Discord](https://discord.gg/CdtchD5zxr) and [GitHub](https://github.com/Alaydriem/bedrock-voice-chat/discussions).

## How we use the money

Your support pays for server costs, app improvements and new platform releases. It also pays for the reverse-engineering work that updates BVC for each Minecraft release. This work keeps BVC working on Realms and Aternos.

# For players

> Install BVC, sign in, and use proximity voice chat on a server that already has it.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/player

This page is for players who want to join a server that already has Bedrock Voice Chat (BVC) set up.

## Getting Started

1. [Install the app](/wiki/start/downloads/) on your device.
2. Join the Minecraft server in game one time.
3. [Sign in](/wiki/player/signing-in/) with the Xbox account that you play on. Use the server URL that your server operator gave you.
4. Put on your headphones and play.

:::caution
Bedrock Voice Chat lets you sign in only after the server knows you. If you cannot sign in, join the Minecraft server in game one time, then try again. If you still cannot sign in, ask your server operator to add you.
:::

If nothing works, the server may not have BVC set up. Send your server operator the [Running a server](/wiki/server/) page.

## Player guides

| Page | Contents |
|---|---|
| [Using voice chat](/wiki/player/using-voice-chat/) | Voice range, mute and deafen, volume for each player. |
| [Groups](/wiki/player/groups/) | Talk to your friends at any distance. |
| [Chat](/wiki/player/chat/) | Read and send in-game chat from the app. |
| [In-game commands](/wiki/player/in-game-commands/) | Control BVC from inside Minecraft with `/bvc` commands. |
| [Using the jukebox](/wiki/player/using-the-jukebox/) | Play audio clips from a block in the world. |
| [Audio library](/wiki/player/audio-library/) | Upload and manage the clips that discs play. |
| [Settings](/wiki/player/settings/) | Devices, noise gate, keybinds, push-to-talk. |
| [Parents and age settings](/wiki/player/parents-and-age/) | Age checks on Android and iOS. |
| [Troubleshooting](/wiki/player/troubleshooting/) | "I cannot hear anyone." |

---

# Audio library

> Upload and manage the audio clips that BVC discs play.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/player/audio-library

The audio library of Bedrock Voice Chat keeps audio clips on the BVC server. Any player can put a clip on a disc and play it in a [jukebox](/wiki/player/using-the-jukebox/).

Open **Settings → Audio library**.

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/settings-audio-library.jpg" alt="Audio Library settings page with several uploaded clips" /></div>

## Permissions

| Action | Permission |
|---|---|
| Play a clip | None. Any player can make a disc. |
| Upload | `audio_upload` |
| Delete | `audio_delete` |

The server operator sets these permissions for all players, and can change them for one player. If the upload button does nothing, ask your server operator for the permission.

## Upload a clip

When you upload a clip, the server gives it an ID. To get a disc for the clip, type `/bvc:disc <audio_id>` with that ID.

Clips are stored on the server. All players on the server use the same library. All players can play a clip that you upload.

## For operators

See [players and permissions](/wiki/server/players-and-permissions/) and the [`audio` configuration](/wiki/reference/configuration/#audio). On a public server, set `audio_upload = false` as the default and give it to players you trust.

---

# Chat

> Read and send in-game chat from the BVC app, without leaving what you are doing.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/player/chat

Bedrock Voice Chat shows the in-game chat of your server in the app. You can read and reply to chat without leaving what you are doing. The messages that you type go into the game as normal chat messages.

## Send a message

1. Open the chat panel on the dashboard.
2. Type your message.
3. Press Enter.

Your message shows in game as `<yourname> your message`.

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/chat-open.jpg" alt="BVC Chat Window" /></div>

## Where your message goes

If you are in a Minecraft world, Bedrock Voice Chat sends your message to that world.

If you are signed in to BVC but you are not in a Minecraft world, BVC can show a list of worlds. The list shows when the server has more than one world that you were in before. Select a world from the list. Each world has two labels:

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Active** | Players are in the world now. |
| **Available** | Chat to this world works now. |

:::caution
A world can be **Active** but not **Available**. The game server is running, but its chat connection to Bedrock Voice Chat does not work. Your message **will not send** to that world.
:::

## A message does not send

**You changed worlds.** You went to a different world, but the app still had the old world selected. Send the message again.

**The message did not send.** You are not connected, the chat connection does not work, or too many messages are waiting. When the chat panel shows chat as available, send the message again.

## History

Chat history starts when you connect and ends when you close the app. The server and your device do not save it.

## Chat is not available

The message box shows the reason:

- **Not connected.** Sign in to a server first.
- **The server has no BVC Addon or mod.** If you connect directly to a Minecraft server, that server needs the BVC Addon or mod. If you connect to a Realm or with Bedrock Voice Chat Connect, it does not.
- **The chat connection is down.** Wait. The mod connects again automatically.
- **Chat is disabled on this server.** The server owner turned chat off. The chat panel stays on your dashboard, greyed out, and you cannot type in it. You cannot turn it on from the app.

## For server operators

Chat needs no setup on the BVC server. To turn chat off, see [`server.features`](/wiki/reference/configuration/#serverfeatures). For the game server setup, see the [Bedrock Addon](/wiki/server/bedrock-addon/), [Fabric](/wiki/server/java-mod/fabric/#chat-sync) or [PaperMC](/wiki/server/java-mod/papermc/#chat-sync) page.

## Privacy

The BVC server sends chat messages and does not store them. It stores a list of the worlds where it saw each player. Each entry has the player, the world, and the time. BVC uses this list to show the world list.

All players in the world can read your messages.

---

# Groups

> Talk to your party at full volume regardless of distance, and keep a group private.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/player/groups

In a group, each member hears all other members at full volume, wherever they are in the world.

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/dashboard-group.jpg" alt="Group panel in the sidebar on the left, showing members" /></div>

## Create a group

Select **New group** in the sidebar on the left, or type `/bvc:groupcreate` in game. In the app, you join the new group and the group editor opens, so you can change its name.

You own each group that you create. When you leave your group, you still own it, and you can join it again. A [Private Group](#private-groups) is different.

There is no limit on the number of groups.

## Join a group

You can join a group in these ways:

- In the app, select the group name in the sidebar.
- On Bedrock, type `/bvc:panel` and join from the panel.
- In game, type `/bvc:groupjoin <code>`.

:::caution
A group that is not a Private Group is open. Any player on the server can join it at any time.
:::

## Leave or close a group

To leave a group, select the group that you are in, or swipe the group to the left and select **Leave**.

If you own the group, swipe it to the left and select **Close** to close it. The group ends for all members.

## Groups and proximity

In a group, you hear all group members at full volume. You also hear players near you. Their volume changes with distance.

In a Private Group, players near you cannot hear you. You still hear them.

## Private Groups

A Private Group is end-to-end encrypted. The BVC server cannot hear what its members say.

A player cannot join a Private Group alone. A member who is online must admit each new player. The new player and the member both see the same 8-digit code in the BVC app, and both confirm that it matches.

A Private Group has a lock next to its name in the sidebar. On Bedrock, the panel shows it as `[Ask] <name>`.

### Make a group private

1. Select **New group**. The group editor opens.
2. Turn on **Private Group**.
3. Select **Save**.

To change a group that you already own, swipe the group to the left and select **Edit**.

Only the owner can make a group private, and only while the owner is the only member. If another player joins first, the app shows "Someone joined. Turn this on while you are alone."

You cannot make a Private Group open again. To have an open group, create a new group.

### Ask to join a Private Group

1. Select the group in the sidebar. On a phone, tap it.
2. Select **Ask to join**. The app shows **Waiting for a member**.
3. When a member checks your request, the app shows an 8-digit code.
4. Read all 8 digits to the member who is checking.
5. Select **It matches** only when the member tells you that their code is the same. If it is not the same, select **No match**.

When the member admits you, you join the group.

Compare the code in person, by phone, or on a voice call that BVC does not carry, for example Discord. Do not type the code in game chat.

A request ends after 2 minutes. When it ends, the app shows one of these titles. Select **Ask again** to send a new request.

| Title | Cause |
|---|---|
| **{member} did not admit you** | The member selected **Deny**. |
| **The codes did not match** | You or the member saw a different code. |
| **No member answered** | No member checked your request in time. |
| **No member is online** | No member of the group is online. |

### Ask to join from the game

You can ask to join a Private Group from the game. The code shows only in the BVC app, never in game.

- On Bedrock, type `/bvc:panel`, open **Groups** and select the `[Ask]` row. You can also type `/bvc:groupjoin <code>`.
- On Java, type `/bvc group join <code>`.

The game replies `Your code for <name> is in the BVC app.` Continue in the app from step 2 above. If the BVC app is not open and signed in, the game replies `Open the BVC app to join <name>.`

Asking to join from the game, from the Stream Deck, or from the [WebSocket API](/wiki/creator/websocket-api/) removes you from your current group first, without a confirmation.

### Admit a player

When a player asks to join your Private Group, the app plays a short tone and shows a card: **Admit {player} to {group}?** On desktop, the cards are at the top right of the dashboard, under **Join requests**. On a phone, they open as a sheet. The tone follows the [Mute cues](/wiki/player/settings/#mute-cues) setting.

1. Select **Check code**. The app shows an 8-digit code.
2. Ask the player to read their code to you.
3. Select **Admit {player}** only if it is that player and the code matches. If not, select **Deny**.

The player then confirms on their side, and joins the group.

A check ends after 60 seconds. Select **Not now** to hide a request. It stays until it ends.

Any member who is online can check a request. When another member checks it, your card shows **{member} is checking {player}**.

You can check up to 3 players at the same time. Only one code shows at a time. Select **Show code** on a card to see its code.

If a card shows **Check failed**, do not admit that player. The check could not confirm who sent the request.

:::caution
A name on a card comes from the server. Admit a player only if you know who is reading the code to you.
:::

### Safety code

All members of a Private Group see the same safety code. The code changes when a member joins or leaves.

While you are in a Private Group, the top of the group list shows "Players nearby cannot hear you." To see the code, select **Safety code** on that line. Read it out to the other members. If your code is different, leave the group.

### Leave a Private Group

When you leave a Private Group, the app asks you to confirm:

- **Leave {group}?** To come back, a member must admit you. This applies to the owner too.
- **Close {group}?** You are the last member. If you leave, the group closes.

The app asks when you select the group, select **Leave**, move to another group, or ask to join another Private Group.

---

# In-game commands

> Control BVC from inside Minecraft without alt-tabbing.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/player/in-game-commands

The Bedrock Addon and the Java mod let you control BVC with commands in the chat bar. You can also use these commands in scripted events.

The commands are different on each edition:

- **[Bedrock](/wiki/player/in-game-commands/bedrock/)**: commands start with `/bvc:`. Example: `/bvc:mute true`
- **[Java](/wiki/player/in-game-commands/java/)**: commands start with `/bvc` and a space. Example: `/bvc mute true`

## Commands on both editions

All players can use every command. No command needs cheats or operator status.

The BVC app must be open and signed in. The commands control the app.

| Action | Bedrock | Java |
|---|---|---|
| Mute yourself | `/bvc:mute <true\|false>` | `/bvc mute <true\|false>` |
| Deafen yourself | `/bvc:deafen <true\|false>` | `/bvc deafen <true\|false>` |
| Start or stop recording | `/bvc:record <true\|false>` | `/bvc record <true\|false>` |
| Set a player's volume | `/bvc:volume <player> <0-150>` | `/bvc volume <player> <0-150>` |
| Hear a player or not | `/bvc:hear <player> <true\|false>` | `/bvc hear <player> <true\|false>` |
| Mute jukebox music | `/bvc:jukeboxmute <true\|false>` | `/bvc jukebox mute <true\|false>` |
| Set jukebox volume | `/bvc:jukeboxvolume <0-150>` | `/bvc jukebox volume <0-150>` |
| Create a group | `/bvc:groupcreate` | `/bvc group create` |
| Join a group | `/bvc:groupjoin <code>` | `/bvc group join <code>` |
| Leave a group | `/bvc:groupleave` | `/bvc group leave` |
| Get an audio disc | `/bvc:disc <audio_id>` | `/bvc disc <audio_id>` |
| Open a control panel | `/bvc:panel` | None |

:::note
The control panel is only on Bedrock. On Java, use the app window.
:::

Volume, hear, and the jukebox commands change only what you hear. When you make a player quieter, other players hear no change, and that player can still hear you.

To join a [Private Group](/wiki/player/groups/#private-groups), a member must admit you in the BVC app. The join command starts the request, and the app shows the code.

Recording is available only on desktop. You can type the command on all devices. It does nothing on a device that cannot record, or on a server that has [turned recording off](/wiki/creator/recording/).

---

# Bedrock commands

> The /bvc: commands and the in-game control panel on Bedrock.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/player/in-game-commands/bedrock

On Bedrock, all BVC commands start with `/bvc:`. Type `/bvc:` and the game shows the list of commands.

These commands need the [Bedrock Addon](/wiki/server/bedrock-addon/) on the server. The BVC app must be open and signed in.

## The panel

```
/bvc:panel
```

This command opens a form with the same controls as the app: mute, deafen, record, jukebox music, and the volume of each player.

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/mc-bvc-panel.jpg" alt="The /bvc:panel control panel open in-game" /></div>

## Your own audio

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `/bvc:mute <true\|false>` | Mutes or unmutes your microphone. |
| `/bvc:deafen <true\|false>` | Deafens or undeafens you. When you are deafened, you hear no one. |
| `/bvc:record <true\|false>` | Starts or stops recording. Desktop only. |

## Other players

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `/bvc:volume <player> <0-150>` | Sets the volume of one player for you. |
| `/bvc:hear <player> <true\|false>` | Sets whether you hear that player. |

These settings change only what you hear. They do not change what other players hear.

At 100, a player plays at normal volume. To make a quiet player louder, set a value above 100. The maximum is 150. The volume slider for each player in the app has the same range.

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/mc-player-volumes.jpg" alt="The Player volumes form, with the Jukebox music row above the player list" /></div>

## Jukebox music

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `/bvc:jukeboxmute <true\|false>` | Mutes or unmutes jukebox music. |
| `/bvc:jukeboxvolume <0-150>` | Sets the volume of jukebox music. |

This setting applies to all jukeboxes at the same time. It changes only what you hear. It does not change the volume of voices.

The panel has the same two controls on its **Jukebox music** row. See [using the jukebox](/wiki/player/using-the-jukebox/).

## Groups

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `/bvc:groupcreate` | Creates a group and shows its share code. |
| `/bvc:groupjoin <code>` | Joins a group with its code. For a Private Group, asks to join in the BVC app. |
| `/bvc:groupleave` | Leaves your current group. |

Tell other players the share code, or paste it in chat. See [Groups](/wiki/player/groups/).

In the **Groups** form of the panel, a Private Group shows as `[Ask] <name>`. Select it to ask to join. A member must admit you in the BVC app, after you both compare a code there. The game replies `Your code for <name> is in the BVC app.` If the app is not open and signed in, it replies `Open the BVC app to join <name>.` See [Ask to join from the game](/wiki/player/groups/#ask-to-join-from-the-game).

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/mc-groups.jpg" alt="The Groups form, listing groups with the current group's share code" /></div>

## Audio discs

```
/bvc:disc <audio_id>
```

This command gives you a disc that plays a clip from the [audio library](/wiki/player/audio-library/). See [using the jukebox](/wiki/player/using-the-jukebox/).

---

# Java commands

> The /bvc commands on Fabric and PaperMC servers.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/player/in-game-commands/java

On Java, all BVC commands start with `/bvc` and a space. Type `/bvc ` and press Tab to complete the rest.

These commands need the [Java mod](/wiki/server/java-mod/) on a Fabric or PaperMC server. The BVC app must be open and signed in. The commands are the same on Fabric and PaperMC.

## Your own audio

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `/bvc mute <true\|false>` | Mutes or unmutes your microphone. |
| `/bvc deafen <true\|false>` | Deafens or undeafens you. When you are deafened, you hear no one. |
| `/bvc record <true\|false>` | Starts or stops recording. Desktop only. |

## Other players

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `/bvc volume <player> <0-150>` | Sets the volume of one player for you. |
| `/bvc hear <player> <true\|false>` | Sets whether you hear that player. |

These settings change only what you hear. When you make a player quieter, other players hear no change, and that player can still hear you.

At 100, a player plays at normal volume. To make a quiet player louder, set a value above 100. The maximum is 150. The volume slider for each player in the app has the same range.

## Jukebox music

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `/bvc jukebox mute <true\|false>` | Mutes or unmutes jukebox music. |
| `/bvc jukebox volume <0-150>` | Sets the volume of jukebox music. |

This setting applies to all jukeboxes at the same time. It changes only what you hear. It does not change the volume of voices.

These are the same two controls as **Settings → Audio settings** in the app. See [using the jukebox](/wiki/player/using-the-jukebox/).

## Groups

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `/bvc group create` | Creates a group and shows its share code. |
| `/bvc group join <code>` | Joins a group with its code. For a Private Group, asks to join in the BVC app. |
| `/bvc group leave` | Leaves your current group. |

For a Private Group, a member must admit you in the BVC app, after you both compare a code there. The game replies `Your code for <name> is in the BVC app.` If the app is not open and signed in, it replies `Open the BVC app to join <name>.` See [Ask to join from the game](/wiki/player/groups/#ask-to-join-from-the-game).

## Audio discs

```
/bvc disc <audio_id>
```

This command gives you a disc that plays a clip from the [audio library](/wiki/player/audio-library/). See [using the jukebox](/wiki/player/using-the-jukebox/).

Only a player can run `/bvc disc`. To give a disc from the server console, use this command:

```
/bvc give <player> <audio_id>
```

## Admin

These commands are for server operators. You can run them only from the server console. Players and command blocks cannot run or see them.

They need the [embedded server](/wiki/server/java-mod/#external-or-embedded-server). With an external server, run [`admin bootstrap`](/wiki/server/players-and-permissions/#bootstrapping-the-first-admin) on the BVC host.

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `/bvc admin grant <gamertag>` | Gives the player the `admin` permission. Creates the player if BVC does not know them. |
| `/bvc admin revoke <gamertag>` | Removes the `admin` setting for this player. The [server-wide default](/wiki/server/players-and-permissions/#server-wide-defaults) then applies. |
| `/bvc admin deny <gamertag>` | Refuses `admin` to the player, even when the default allows it. |

`<gamertag>` is the Xbox gamertag that the player uses to sign in to BVC. It can be different from their name in game. It is case-sensitive. If it contains a space, put it in quotes:

```
/bvc admin grant "Some Name"
```

`grant` creates the player record. After this, the player can also sign in to BVC. `revoke` and `deny` change only existing players. If BVC does not know the gamertag, the command shows `<gamertag> is not a BVC player; nothing was changed.`

---

# Parents and age settings

> How Age Signals on Android and Declared Age Ranges on iOS work, and how to change them.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/player/parents-and-age

Bedrock Voice Chat (BVC) uses Age Signals on Android and Declared Age Ranges on iOS. These are age checks from Google and Apple. Parents decide if their child uses voice chat on the servers that the child plays on.

## What BVC is

Bedrock Voice Chat is a voice chat app for Minecraft Bedrock and Java. Players hear other players who are near them in the game. Players on different devices can talk to each other.

:::caution[Who runs the server your child connects to]
Bedrock Voice Chat is software. Other people install it on their own Minecraft servers. We do not run these servers. Each server belongs to a Minecraft community, for example a friend, a school group, or a Discord community.

The person who runs the server (the operator) decides which players can join, and sets the minimum age. We cannot see who is on these servers, and we cannot moderate them. If something goes wrong on a server, contact its operator.
:::

## What information is collected

**The app sends your child's gamertag and profile picture URL to the server that they connect to.** Other players see who is speaking, and the app shows names and pictures in the player list.

This information goes to the operator's server. It does not go to us. The operator decides what to do with it.

Bedrock Voice Chat collects only anonymous analytics: diagnostic logs, error logs, and some usage events. We use this data only to improve the app. None of it identifies you or your child. The operator can [turn it off](/wiki/server/privacy-and-telemetry/).

BVC never stores or sends your child's age. BVC asks Apple or Google if the signed-in user meets the minimum age of the server. Apple or Google answers only yes or no.

See the full policy: [PRIVACY_STATEMENT.md](https://github.com/Alaydriem/bedrock-voice-chat/blob/master/PRIVACY_STATEMENT.md).

## Who your child can talk to

Your child can talk to all players on the server. The operator sets a minimum age for the server, and BVC applies it. The community decides who plays on its server. Often it is a group of friends from school. Sometimes it is a larger online community.

The operator is a member of the community, and each community has different rules. Some servers have careful moderation and some do not. Find out who your child plays with. Agree together on what is safe to share online.

## Block someone

You can mute a player in the app. Your child then does not hear that player, even when the player is near. The muted player can still hear your child.

If a player behaves badly, contact the server operator. Bad behaviour usually breaks the rules of the community, and the community's moderators can act on it.

## When the age warning appears

The age warning appears only when both of these are true:

1. The server operator has set a minimum age.
2. Your device and Google or Apple account are in a region that requires Age Signals or Declared Age Ranges.

If either is false, no warning appears.

## If no age warning appears

Your child cannot use voice chat on a server until the operator of that server adds them, or until your child joins the server in Minecraft.

To stop all use of the app, use the parental controls and app restrictions on the device.

### Limit to specific servers

You cannot limit BVC to specific servers at this time. To ask for this feature, open a GitHub issue or ask on Discord.

## Change the setting

You cannot change this setting in BVC. BVC asks Google or Apple if the signed-in user is old enough for the server. To change the answer, change the parental controls on the Google or Apple account.

After you change the parental controls, restart BVC. The app checks again when it starts.

### Android

Age Signals come from the Google account on the device, and from Family Link supervision.

1. Open the child's profile in **Family Link**.
2. Check the birth date. A wrong birth date is the usual cause of an unexpected block.
3. If Google asks for consent for this app, give it. Google asks for consent when a supervised account uses an app that lets users talk to other people.

If the account is not supervised and the birth date is correct, the cause of the block is the minimum age that the operator set. Ask the operator what age they set.

Google's help: [Family Link Help](https://support.google.com/families).

### iOS

Declared Age Ranges come from the date of birth of the Apple Account, and from Family Sharing.

1. Open the child's account under **Settings → Family**.
2. Check the date of birth.
3. Open **Screen Time → Content & Privacy Restrictions**. When iOS asks, allow access to the declared age range.

If the account is not in a Family Sharing group and the date of birth is correct, the cause of the block is the minimum age that the operator set. Ask the operator what age they set.

Apple's help: [Family Sharing](https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT201060).

## For operators

See [Minimum age](/wiki/server/privacy-and-telemetry/#minimum-age).

---

# Settings

> Audio devices, noise gate, keybinds, and the rest of the settings panes.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/player/settings

Bedrock Voice Chat has settings for audio devices, voice mode, the noise gate, keybinds, and more.

## Audio settings

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/settings-audio.jpg" alt="Audio settings page showing input and output device selection" /></div>

### Devices

By default, BVC uses the default communication device and speaker of your computer or phone. To use a different microphone or speaker, select it from the list.

On Windows, BVC works with standard audio devices and with ASIO devices (professional audio interfaces).

### Test your devices

- **Test my microphone.** Speak for a few seconds. The bar fills when BVC hears you. If the bar does not move, select a different input device.
- **Test playback.** BVC plays a chime through the output device.

### Voice mode

BVC has two voice modes:

- **Open mic** sends your voice when you speak loudly enough to open the noise gate.
- **Push to talk** sends your voice only while you hold the push-to-talk key. Set the key under [Keybinds](#keybinds).

### Mute cues

BVC plays a short tone when you mute or deafen, and a different tone when you unmute or undeafen. It also plays a tone when a player asks to join your [Private Group](/wiki/player/groups/#admit-a-player). This setting is on by default.

### Spatial panning

Spatial panning sets how much BVC moves a voice to the left or right, based on where the player stands. At 0%, all voices are in the centre. The volume still changes with distance.

### Jukeboxes

This setting has one volume control and one mute for all jukeboxes in the world. It does not change the volume of voices. See [using the jukebox](/wiki/player/using-the-jukebox/).

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/settings-audio-more.jpg" alt="Audio settings page showing voice chat sounds, jukebox volume, and the noise gate toggle" /></div>

### Noise gate

BVC has a noise gate that works like the noise gate in OBS. The default settings block the noise from fans, keyboards, and mouse clicks.

If you already use other noise suppression (for example, VST plug-ins or the noise suppression of your operating system), turn off this noise gate. Two noise gates together make your voice sound worse.

| Control | Effect |
|---|---|
| Open Threshold | The level that your voice must go above to open the gate. |
| Close Threshold | The level that your voice must go below to close the gate. Set it below the open threshold. |
| Attack Rate | How fast the gate opens after your voice goes above the threshold. |
| Hold Time | How long the gate stays open after your voice goes below the threshold. This stops the gate from cutting off your voice between words. |
| Release Rate | How fast the gate closes after the hold time ends. |

## Keybinds

Keybinds are keyboard shortcuts. They work while Minecraft is the active window.

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/settings-keybinds.jpg" alt="Keybinds settings page listing mute, deafen, recording, and push to talk" /></div>

| Action | Notes |
|---|---|
| Toggle Mute | |
| Toggle Deafen | |
| Toggle Recording | Desktop only. |
| Push to Talk | Sends your voice only while you hold the key. |

## Player audio levels

**Player audio levels** lists all players that you have heard. Each player has a volume control and a mute. Your changes stay after a player walks away. Only you hear the changes.

Use the search box to find a player in a long list. **Reset everybody** sets all players back to full volume and unmutes them.

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/settings-players.jpg" alt="Player audio levels page listing players with a volume slider and mute for each" /></div>

## Recordings

See your recorded sessions, rename them, and export the audio of each player to a separate file (BWAV or MP4/Opus). See [Recording](/wiki/creator/recording/).

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/settings-recordings.jpg" alt="Recordings settings page listing recent sessions" /></div>

## Language

The language setting is on the **About** page. Select a language, or **Match my system**. Text that is not translated stays in English.

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/settings-about.jpg" alt="About page showing build information, display language, and diagnostics" /></div>

## Other settings

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/settings-account.jpg" alt="Account page showing the signed-in identity and linked accounts" /></div>

| Page | Contents |
|---|---|
| Account | Your signed-in identity and connected servers. |
| Audio library | Upload and manage audio clips. Needs the `audio_upload` permission. See [audio library](/wiki/player/audio-library/). |
| WebSocket server | Lets other apps on your computer control BVC. The [Stream Deck plugin](/wiki/creator/stream-deck/) uses it. |
| About | Version, build information, language, and diagnostics. |

Under **Minecraft Bedrock**:

| Page | Contents |
|---|---|
| Voice Chat Connect | Connect to a Realm, or to Aternos and other hosts that use the no-net Addon. Select the world from the list. See [Realms](/wiki/platforms/realms/) and [Aternos](/wiki/platforms/aternos/). |

Recordings and Keybinds are available only on desktop.

---

# Signing in

> Connect the BVC app to a server with your Xbox account.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/player/signing-in

Sign in to Bedrock Voice Chat with your Microsoft (Xbox) account. BVC uses this account to identify you on your server.

:::tip
The servers that you connect to store your gamertag and profile picture. Bedrock Voice Chat itself collects only anonymous analytics (diagnostic logs, error logs and event tracking) to improve the app. See [What information is collected](/wiki/player/parents-and-age/#what-information-is-collected).
:::

## Join the Minecraft server first

Join your Minecraft server in game before you sign in to Bedrock Voice Chat. BVC lets you sign in after the Minecraft server sends you to BVC.

:::caution
If you play on a Realm, or on Aternos with the no-net Addon, your server operator **MUST** add you on the BVC server **FIRST**. Then you can sign in.
:::

## Your server URL

The server URL is the address of the **BVC server**. It is not the address of your Minecraft server, your Aternos server, or your Realm. It is not the IP address that you type in Minecraft.

The URL starts with `https://`, followed by the full server name:

```
https://example.bedrockvc.stream
```

Your server operator gives you this address.

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/signing-in-login.jpg" alt="BVC login window with the server URL field filled in" /></div>

## Sign in

1. Enter the URL.
2. Sign in on the Microsoft page that opens. Use the account of the gamertag that you play with on that server.
3. Wait while BVC checks your sign-in and connects.

BVC shows the dashboard. Put on your headphones and play.

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/signing-in-dashboard.jpg" alt="BVC dashboard immediately after a successful sign-in" /></div>

---

# Troubleshooting

> What to check when BVC is not working.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/player/troubleshooting

## I cannot sign in

**`AUTH02`, or "not whitelisted".** Join the Minecraft server in game one time, then sign in again. If you still cannot sign in, ask your server operator to add you.

**BVC does not accept the URL.** You are probably using the Minecraft server address. The server URL is the address of the **BVC server**. See [signing in](/wiki/player/signing-in/).

**Sign-in does not finish.** The BVC server may be down. Ask your server operator to check that the BVC server is running.

## I signed in but hear nobody

Do these checks in order.

1. **Do other players use BVC?** All players need the app open and signed in.
2. **Are you near other players?** By default, you hear players at full volume up to 24 blocks away. At 48 blocks, you hear nothing. Stand next to a player.
3. **Are you deafened?** Check the deafen button at the bottom left. Also check the mute button on each player in the player list.
4. **Is your output device correct?** Open **Settings → Audio settings** and select **Test playback**. If you do not hear a chime, select a different output device.
5. **Do you play on Realms or Aternos?** Connect with **Voice Chat Connect** in the app. If you connect to the server address directly, BVC does not work.

## Nobody can hear me

**Are you muted?** Check the mute button at the bottom left.

**Do you use push-to-talk?** If you set a push-to-talk key, BVC sends your voice only while you hold that key. Open **Settings → Keybinds**.

**Is your input device correct?** Open **Settings → Audio settings** and select **Test my microphone**. Speak for a few seconds. If the bar does not move, select a different input device.

**Is the noise gate too strong?** If you speak quietly or are far from the microphone, the gate may never open. Lower the open threshold, or turn the gate off to test. See [Settings](/wiki/player/settings/).

## Audio cuts in and out

Usually, the noise gate closes between your words. Increase the hold time.

If the noise gate is not the cause, the cause is probably your network. Some networks slow down or block the connection that BVC uses for voice. Try a different network, then ask your server operator.

## The record button does nothing

**Are you on a phone?** Recording is available only on desktop.

**Did your server turn recording off?** Server operators can turn off recording. The app then does not start a recording from the button, from `/bvc:record`, or from the Stream Deck. Ask your server operator. See [recording](/wiki/creator/recording/).

## I cannot export an old recording

You can export a recording only if it uses the same recording format as your app. A BVC update can change this format. After the update, old recordings stay on your device and in the list, but you cannot export them.

Export the recordings that you want to keep before you update. See [recording](/wiki/creator/recording/#format-version).

## It worked yesterday

**Did Minecraft update?** On Realms or Aternos, a Minecraft update stops voice chat until a BVC version for that Minecraft version is available. See [version support](/wiki/platforms/version-support/).

**Did you update BVC?** `VER01` means that your app is older than the server. `VER02` means that the server is older than your app. You can see the versions in **Settings → About**.

## Error codes

Give the code when you ask for help.

| Code | Meaning | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTH02` | The server does not know you yet. | Join the Minecraft server in game one time, or ask the operator to add you. |
| `AUTH01` | The server could not confirm who you are. | Sign in again. |
| `AUTH03` | This device could not save your sign-in. | Try again. If it happens again, restart the device. |
| `AUTH04` | This device has no unlocked keyring (password storage) for your sign-in. | See [secure storage](#secure-storage). |
| `CONN01` | BVC cannot connect to the server. | Ask your server operator. |
| `QUIC01` | BVC connected to the server, but the voice connection failed. | Your network may block voice. Try a different network, then ask your server operator. |
| `DNS01` | BVC could not find the server address. | Check the address for a typing error. |
| `CERT01` | The server's security certificate changed after you signed in. | Sign in again. BVC deleted your saved sign-in for this server. If this happens again, ask your server operator. |
| `CERT02` | BVC cannot confirm the security of the voice connection. | Ask your server operator. Only the operator can fix this. Your sign-in is kept. |
| `VER01` | Your app is older than the server. | Update the app. |
| `VER02` | The server is older than your app. | Ask your server operator to update. |
| `AUDI01` `AUDI02` `AUDI03` | An input or output device is missing or does not work. | Open **Settings → Audio settings**. |
| `PERM1` | BVC does not have permission to use the microphone. | Allow microphone access in your system settings, then go back to the dashboard. |
| `PERM2` | BVC does not have permission to show notifications. | Allow notifications in your system settings, then go back to the dashboard. On mobile, BVC needs this permission to play audio in the background. |
| `SERV01` | The background audio service could not start. | Mobile only. Make sure that your system does not limit the app in the background. |
| `AGE01` | An adult must finish the setup of this account. | See [parents and age settings](/wiki/player/parents-and-age/). |

`AUTH02` does not mean that something is broken. The server has not added you yet.

## Secure storage

Bedrock Voice Chat saves your sign-in for each server in the password storage of your operating system. `AUTH03` and `AUTH04` mean that you signed in correctly, but BVC could not save the sign-in. BVC cannot finish the sign-in without it.

`AUTH03` means that your operating system did not let BVC save the sign-in. This problem usually stops by itself. Try again. If it continues, restart the device.

`AUTH04` means that your computer has no unlocked keyring (password storage). This error occurs on Linux. To fix it:

1. Open **Passwords and Keys** (`seahorse`).
2. Create a password keyring with the name **Login**.
3. Set it as the default keyring.

If your computer logs you in automatically when it starts, no keyring is unlocked. Turn off automatic login. Then log in to your computer with your password one time. This creates and unlocks the keyring.

## Still stuck

Before you ask for help, collect this information:

- The BVC server address.
- Your device and operating system.
- The error code.
- If BVC works for other players on the server.
- The fixes that you already tried.

Ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/CdtchD5zxr) or open a [GitHub issue](https://github.com/Alaydriem/bedrock-voice-chat/issues).

---

# Using the jukebox

> Play audio clips in-world through the BVC audio player block.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/player/using-the-jukebox

The Jukebox feature of Bedrock Voice Chat lets you play your own audio files in your world. Players near the jukebox hear it louder than players far away. You can use it for scripted games, for example a Decked Out style game that you build with redstone and hoppers.

To use the jukebox, you need three things:

1. A clip in the server's [audio library](/wiki/player/audio-library/).
2. A BVC disc for that clip.
3. A BVC audio player block to put the disc in.

## Get a disc

```
/bvc:disc <audio_id>
```

`audio_id` is the ID of the clip in the audio library. You get a music disc with the name `BVC: <audio_id>`.

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/mc-disc.jpg" alt="A BVC disc in the hotbar, with its BVC: audio_id name visible" /></div>

## Craft the audio player

### Bedrock

On Bedrock Edition, craft the BVC Audio Player first.

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/mc-audio-player-recipe.jpg" alt="Crafting recipe for the BVC audio player block" /></div>

### Java

On Java Edition, use the normal Minecraft jukebox.

## Play a clip

1. Place the block.
2. Put the disc in.

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/mc-jukebox.jpg" alt="A jukebox placed in the world, with a BVC disc in hand" /></div>

All players in range hear the clip through BVC. The clip gets quieter with distance, the same as a voice. See [using voice chat](/wiki/player/using-voice-chat/) for the ranges.

To stop the clip, take the disc out. If the server restarts, the clip starts to play again.

## Volume

Open **Settings → Audio settings** to set one volume for all jukeboxes, or to mute all of them. The volume of voices does not change.

To change the volume in game, use these commands:

| Bedrock | Java |
|---|---|
| `/bvc:jukeboxmute <true\|false>` | `/bvc jukebox mute <true\|false>` |
| `/bvc:jukeboxvolume <0-150>` | `/bvc jukebox volume <0-150>` |

On Bedrock, the **Jukebox music** row of `/bvc:panel` has both controls.

:::caution
All players **MUST** have the BVC app open and connected to hear a jukebox. A player without the app hears nothing.

A disc can play only a clip from the server's library. It cannot play a web link or a file on your device. To add clips, you need the `audio_upload` permission. See [audio library](/wiki/player/audio-library/).
:::

One player can play a maximum of 5 clips at the same time. The server operator can change this limit.

## For operators

The audio player block and the disc command come from the Addon or the Java mod. To change where clips are stored, or the maximum number of clips for each player, see the [`audio` configuration](/wiki/reference/configuration/#audio). To control who can add and delete clips, see [players and permissions](/wiki/server/players-and-permissions/).

---

# Using voice chat

> Proximity ranges, muting, deafening, and per-player volume.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/player/using-voice-chat

Bedrock Voice Chat lets you hear people near you in the world, and people in groups that you create or join.

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/dashboard-group.jpg" alt="BVC dashboard showing the player list with proximity and group members" /></div>

## Proximity

BVC uses your position, the direction you face, and the position of each player to put their voice around you. A player on your left sounds like they are on your left.

With the default settings:

| Distance | What you hear |
|---|---|
| 0 to 24 blocks | Full volume. |
| 24 to 48 blocks | The voice gets quieter. At 48 blocks, it is very quiet. |
| More than 48 blocks | Nothing. |

Left-right positioning starts at 8 blocks and increases up to 24 blocks. A player very close to you sounds like they are in front of you.

Server operators can change all of these values. See the `voice.spatial_audio` block in the [configuration reference](/wiki/reference/configuration/#voicespatial_audio).

## Groups

In a group, you hear all group members at full volume, wherever they are. Their voices do not move left or right. You also still hear nearby players, and they still hear you. See [Groups](/wiki/player/groups/).

## Mute and deafen yourself

Both buttons are at the bottom of the sidebar on the left.

**Mute** stops BVC from sending your voice. **Deafen** stops all sound from other players.

You can set a key for each button, and for push-to-talk. See [Settings](/wiki/player/settings/).

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/mute-deafen.jpg" alt="The Mute and Deafen buttons within the app." /></div>

## Adjust another player

You can change the volume of any player who comes near you. You can mute them, or make them louder or quieter.

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/dashboard-earshot.jpg" alt="Adjusting player volume" /></div>

:::tip
Be sure to change a player's volume while they are within 24 blocks of you. At this distance, you hear them at full volume.
:::

:::caution
When you mute a player, only **you** stop hearing them. They can still hear you.
:::

Your changes stay after the player walks away or leaves the game. To find a player who is not on the screen, or to undo a mute, open **Settings → Player audio levels**. It lists every player you have heard, and has a button to reset all of them.

---

# Running a server

> What you need to add BVC to your Minecraft server, and the order to do it in.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/server

To add Bedrock Voice Chat to your Minecraft server, run the BVC server and install one Addon or mod.

## BVC server

The BVC server is a standalone Rust program. Run it in Docker, or run the native binary. It is not a Minecraft plugin and does not run inside your game server. Most commercial Minecraft hosts do not let you run it next to the game server. Run it on a VPS, a dedicated server, or a cluster.

On Bedrock, the game server side is an Addon. On Java, it is a Fabric or Paper mod. The Addon or the mod sends player positions to the BVC server over HTTP.

The Java mod can also run BVC inside the game server's JVM. You then do not need a separate BVC service. Use this for small servers that run all the time. Do not use it on low-end hosts or on hosts that suspend idle servers.

## Installation order

Do these steps in order. If you do them out of order, a new installation can appear to do nothing.

1. [Install the BVC server](/wiki/server/installation/). You need a host that clients can reach, and a TLS certificate. BVC can get and renew the certificate itself. See [TLS](/wiki/server/tls/).
2. Install the [Bedrock Addon](/wiki/server/bedrock-addon/) or the [Java mod](/wiki/server/java-mod/). Set it to the address of the BVC server.
3. Let your players in. A player can sign in after they join your game server once, or after you [add them](/wiki/server/players-and-permissions/).
4. Send your players to [Downloads](/wiki/start/downloads/).

## References

| Page | Contents |
|---|---|
| [BDS Addon](/wiki/server/bedrock-addon/) | The pack for Bedrock Dedicated Servers. |
| [No-net Addon](/wiki/server/nonet-addon/) | The pack for Realms, Aternos, and hosts without `@minecraft/server-net`. |
| [Docker](/wiki/server/docker/) | Compose, volumes, health checks, configuration from environment variables. |
| [Monitoring](/wiki/server/monitoring/) | Prometheus metrics, health endpoints, logs. |
| [Troubleshooting](/wiki/server/troubleshooting/) | Problems seen from the operator side. |

Realms, Aternos and consoles need more setup. Start at [Where BVC works](/wiki/platforms/).

---

# Bedrock Dedicated Server Addon

> Install and configure the BVC Addon on a Bedrock Dedicated Server.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/server/bedrock-addon

The Bedrock Addon sends player positions from your Bedrock Dedicated Server (BDS) to the Bedrock Voice Chat server. Proximity voice chat needs these positions.

:::caution
The Addon is **mandatory**. Without it, Bedrock Voice Chat does not receive player positions, and players cannot hear each other.
:::

This page is for Bedrock Dedicated Server. For Realms, Aternos, and other hosts that do not allow `@minecraft/server-net`, use the [no-net Addon](/wiki/server/nonet-addon/).

Install the [BVC server](/wiki/server/installation/) first. You need its URL and access token for these steps.

## Install

1. Download the latest `.mcaddon` from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Alaydriem/bedrock-voice-chat/releases) or [CurseForge](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft-bedrock/addons/bedrock-voice-chat).

2. Extract it. Copy the `behavior_packs` and `resource_packs` directories into the directories with the same names on your server.

   Do not put the Addon in `worlds/`. If you do, a shared or exported world contains your BVC server URL and access token.

3. Create or edit `config/default/variables.json`:

   ```json
   {
       "bvc_access_token": "<MUST MATCH server.minecraft.access_token>",
       "bvc_server": "https://example.bedrockvc.stream",
       "bvc_minimum_players": 1,
       "bvc_world_name": "My SMP"
   }
   ```

   | Key | Description |
   |---|---|
   | `bvc_access_token` | Must match `server.minecraft.access_token` in `config.hcl`. |
   | `bvc_server` | Public URL of your BVC server. No trailing slash. Include the port if it is not 443. |
   | `bvc_minimum_players` | Number of players who must be online before the Addon sends positions. The default is 1. |
   | `bvc_world_name` | Name of this world in the app's [chat](/wiki/player/chat/) world list. The default is "Minecraft world". |

   Set `bvc_world_name`. BDS scripts cannot read the level name. The app shows only the `bvc_world_name` value.

4. Allow the modules that the Addon uses in `config/default/permissions.json`:

   ```json
   {
       "allowed_modules": [
           "@minecraft/server",
           "@minecraft/server-admin",
           "@minecraft/server-net",
           "@minecraft/server-ui"
       ]
   }
   ```

5. Enable [Beta APIs](/wiki/server/beta-apis/) for your world.

6. Add the packs to your world's behavior pack and resource pack lists. Use the UUID of the variant that you installed. On BDS, this is the Full variant.

   | Variant | Behavior pack UUID |
   |---|---|
   | Full | `6fb24263-357a-407c-aebe-681f50b2de50` |
   | No-net | `508a43ed-b95e-40cf-98eb-d78f2d72caa4` |

   Copy the version from the `manifest.json` file in the pack that you downloaded. The version changes with each release.

7. Start or restart BDS.

## Verify

Set `content-log-console-output-enabled=true` in `server.properties`. When the world loads, the console shows:

```
[BVC] Connecting to: <your server>
```

If the line does not show, the Addon is not running, or `bvc_server` is not set.

Then check that the server receives positions:

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <your token>" https://example.bedrockvc.stream/api/position
```

If the response is empty, BDS does not send positions. If the response lists players, BDS sends positions and the BVC server receives them.

## Other Addon features

The Addon also adds:

- [In-game commands](/wiki/player/in-game-commands/).
- The [jukebox](/wiki/player/using-the-jukebox/) block.
- [Chat](/wiki/player/chat/) sync. Players can read and send in-game chat from the app.

## Troubleshooting

**No `[BVC] Connecting to:` line.** Beta APIs are off, the pack is not in the world's pack list, or a module is missing from `permissions.json`.

**The Addon connects, but nobody hears anyone.** Let your players in. A player can sign in after they join your game server once, or after you add them. See [players and permissions](/wiki/server/players-and-permissions/).

**No positions when you test alone.** `bvc_minimum_players` has a default of 1. If you set a higher value, set it to 1 for the test.

**The BVC server does not respond to `curl`.** The problem is in the BVC server. Go to [installation](/wiki/server/installation/).

---

# Enabling Beta APIs

> Turning on the Beta APIs experiment for a Bedrock server world.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/server/beta-apis

The Bedrock Voice Chat Addon uses beta script modules. You **MUST** enable the **Beta APIs** experiment on the world that runs the Addon.

:::danger
Without Beta APIs, the Addon loads but does nothing. It shows no error and no console line, and it sends no positions.
:::

:::caution[No server.properties setting]
Each world stores its experiments in its own `level.dat` file. A server configuration file cannot enable them. A new world that BDS creates at first start does not have them.
:::

## Create the world in the client

Enable the experiment in the Minecraft client, then move the world to the server.

1. In the Minecraft Bedrock **client**, create a new world.
2. Open **Settings → Experiments** and turn on **Beta APIs**.
3. Add the BVC Addon to the world's behavior packs and resource packs.
4. Create the world, then leave it immediately.
5. Open **Settings**, then select **Export World**. Save the `.mcworld` file.
6. Put the world on your server:
   - **BDS**: rename the file to `.zip`. Extract it into `worlds/<your world name>/`. Set `level-name` in `server.properties` to the same name.
   - **A host with a control panel**: upload the `.mcworld` or `.zip` file with the host's world upload feature.

The [no-net Addon](/wiki/server/nonet-addon/) guide uses the same steps. Realms and Aternos worlds also need Beta APIs.

## Existing worlds

Server settings cannot enable the experiment on an existing world. The setting is in the world's `level.dat`.

There are three methods. The first has the lowest risk.

**Open the world in the client.** Copy the world from the server and open it in the Bedrock client. Enable Beta APIs under Experiments, exit, and copy the world back.

**Use your host's control panel.** Aternos and some other hosts have experiment switches in their control panel. If your host has one, use it.

**Edit `level.dat` with an NBT editor.** The experiment flags are in an `experiments` compound. Set the flag for Beta APIs. Also set the flag that marks the world as a world that uses experiments.

:::caution
The NBT key names change between Bedrock versions. Do not copy a key name from a guide. Create a test world in the client with Beta APIs enabled. Open both `level.dat` files side by side, and copy the differences.
:::

Back up the world before you edit it. A world with a damaged `level.dat` does not load.

## Side effects

**Achievements are permanently disabled** for that world. This applies to every experiment in Minecraft.

**The world is permanently marked as a world that used experiments.** If you turn the experiment off later, the mark stays.

**Experimental features can change between Minecraft versions.**

## Verification

Set this in `server.properties`:

```properties
content-log-console-output-enabled=true
```

When the world loads, this line shows in the console:

```
[BVC] Connecting to: <your server>
```

If the line does not show, the Addon is not running. Check these causes, most likely first:

1. Beta APIs are not enabled on **the world that the server loads**. Check that `level-name` is the world you edited.
2. The Addon is not in the world's pack list.
3. A module is missing from `config/default/permissions.json`. See [Bedrock Addon](/wiki/server/bedrock-addon/).
4. `bvc_server` is not set in `variables.json`.

## Java servers

Java servers do not need Beta APIs. Experiments exist only in Bedrock. See [Java mod](/wiki/server/java-mod/).

---

# Docker and Kubernetes

> Compose, volumes, health checks, and running BVC entirely from environment variables.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/server/docker

Bedrock Voice Chat server ships as a container image at `ghcr.io/alaydriem/bedrock-voice-chat/server`, built for amd64 and arm64.

## Compose

```yaml
services:
  bedrock-voice-chat:
    image: ghcr.io/alaydriem/bedrock-voice-chat/server:<VERSION>
    restart: always
    ports:
      - "443:443/tcp"
      - "28280:28280/udp"
      - "28284:28284/udp"
    user: "100:101"
    cap_add:
      - NET_BIND_SERVICE
    volumes:
      - ./:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-fsS", "https://localhost/health/readiness"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
```

## What to persist

Mount `/data` and keep it. It holds:

- `config.hcl`
- The SQLite database, if you are not using MySQL or Postgres

The database holds the mTLS certificate authority. Losing it invalidates every client certificate already issued and forces everyone to sign in again.

The certificates directory (`server.tls.certs_path`) can be temporary. At startup, the server writes the CA into it from the database. If the directory is empty, the server fills it again. Set `server.tls.certs_path` to a temporary directory if a persistent volume is not practical.

:::caution
Your server's own TLS certificate is different from the mTLS CA. The server reads `server.tls.certificate` and `server.tls.key` from the path where you mount them. They are not stored in the database.
:::

## Running without a config file

Most settings have a `BVC_*` environment variable. You do not need a `config.hcl` file. When there is no `config.hcl`, the server starts with the defaults and the environment variables, and writes a log line that says so.

On Kubernetes, configure BVC with environment variables. Put secret values in Kubernetes Secrets. You do not need a ConfigMap. See [environment variables](/wiki/reference/environment-variables/).

A variable that is not set, or that is empty, does not change a value. `FOO=` in a compose file does not clear a configured value. If a variable has an invalid value, the server does not start.

## Health checks

| Endpoint | Use |
|---|---|
| `/health/liveness` | The process is running. Restart the container if this fails. |
| `/health/readiness` | The server can accept traffic. Use it for the load balancer check. |
| `/api/ping` | A light check that the server is reachable. |

Kubernetes:

```yaml
livenessProbe:
  httpGet: { path: /health/liveness, port: 443, scheme: HTTPS }
  initialDelaySeconds: 30
readinessProbe:
  httpGet: { path: /health/readiness, port: 443, scheme: HTTPS }
  periodSeconds: 10
```

## Graceful shutdown

The server handles SIGTERM. `docker stop` and pod eviction close connections correctly.

## Scaling

BVC is limited by CPU, and each connection keeps state on one instance. Add CPU cores to one instance before you add instances.

Do not put several instances behind an ordinary load balancer. A QUIC connection stays open for a long time and must stay on the instance that opened it. Round-robin routing breaks voice. To share one address between instances, the load balancer must route by QUIC connection ID.

---

# Assigned hostnames

> Getting a hostname and a certificate for a server that has no domain.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/server/enrollment

:::caution[Work in progress. Limited availability.]
Assigned hostnames are in development and are **not in a release yet**. The configuration can change.

Only **some Patreon supporters and YouTube members** can use this feature. A membership alone does not qualify. Only some membership tiers qualify, and these tiers can change during development.
:::

A Bedrock Voice Chat server needs a hostname and a valid certificate. The usual method is to buy a domain, point its DNS at your host, and configure an ACME provider.

Enrollment gives you a hostname without a domain. Bedrock Voice Chat gives you a name under `bedrockvc.stream` and renews a certificate for it. You do not need a domain, DNS settings, or an ACME provider.

You get one name. BVC chooses the name. The name stays with your server while your membership is active and the server keeps its key.

## Requirements

You need a qualifying Patreon or YouTube membership on the Discord account that you sign in with. Patreon and YouTube memberships sync to a Discord role, and BVC checks for that role. A membership that has not synced yet does not qualify.

## Enroll

1. Open the enrollment link that eligible members receive, and sign in with Discord. You get an enrollment token.

2. Put the token in `config.hcl`:

   ```hcl
   server {
       enrollment {
           token = "bvcenroll..."
       }
   }
   ```

3. Start the server. The log shows the name that you got:

   ```
   this server is reachable at its assigned name  url=https://cobblestone-thicket-savanna.bedrockvc.stream
   ```

Do not add a `tls` block. The server adds the assigned name to its certificate and manages the certificate itself. If you add a `tls` block, the server does not start. See [Conflicts](#conflicts).

The server uses the token one time, at first start. After that, the server identifies itself with a key that it makes. You can keep the token in the file or delete it.

:::caution[Back up the server key]
Your server makes a key at first start. The name is linked to that key. If you lose the key, you must enroll again and you get a **different** name. Back up the server's data directory. Keep the directory on a volume that is kept when the container is replaced.
:::

## Address

Set `address` to the IP address that clients connect to. If you do not set it, BVC does not publish a DNS record for your name. Clients then cannot find the server, even though the certificate is valid.

If the server has a name and no address, it writes a warning at startup.

```hcl
server {
    enrollment {
        token   = "bvcenroll..."
        address = "203.0.113.10"
    }
}
```

BVC does not detect the address. Behind NAT, behind CGNAT, or on a LAN, the address that outside servers see is not the address that clients use. A detected address is correct only for a server with port forwarding.

BVC publishes a private address (`192.168.x.x`, `10.x.x.x`). The name then resolves only on the network that set it. BVC checks a public address every day.

## Conflicts

You cannot use an assigned name and your own certificate configuration together. If you set both, the server does not start. The error names the two settings:

```
server.enrollment.token and tls.acme are mutually exclusive; remove one
```

Use one of these:

| Setting | When |
|---|---|
| `server.enrollment` | You have no domain. |
| `tls.acme` | You have a domain and a supported DNS provider. See [TLS certificates](/wiki/server/tls/). |
| `tls.certificate` / `tls.key` | You already have a certificate. |

## Errors

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| `not entitled` | The Discord account that you signed in with does not have a qualifying role. Make sure that your Patreon or YouTube membership has synced. |
| `already registered` | That Discord account already has a name. Each member gets one name. |
| `unknown token` or `already redeemed` | The token was used, typed incorrectly, or is more than one day old. Sign in again to get a new token. |
| A different name after a rebuild | The server's key was lost. Restore the data directory, or use the new name. |
| The name does not resolve | No `address` is set, and BVC did not publish a DNS record. Set `address` and restart the server. |

---

# Installing Bedrock Voice Chat Server

> Install the standalone BVC server with Docker, a configuration file, and automatic TLS.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/server/installation

Bedrock Voice Chat Server is the central part of Bedrock Voice Chat. Bedrock and Java players connect to it to talk to each other. Set up the server before you install the Addon.

## Requirements

1. A Linux server, a Windows computer, or a hosting platform that runs Docker containers.
2. A domain name.
3. A TLS certificate.

:::tip[Hosting providers]
A server with 1 CPU core and 512 MB of memory supports about 5 players at the same time. If audio stutters, add CPU cores, or change to a plan with dedicated CPU cores.

These links support development:

- [DigitalOcean](https://m.do.co/c/15e066af535c): referral credit after you spend $25.
- [Hetzner](https://hetzner.cloud/?ref=StImwLqshuwn): $25 credit when you sign up.
:::

:::tip[Domain registrars]
- [Namecheap](https://www.namecheap.com/)
- [Cloudflare](https://www.cloudflare.com/products/registrar/)
- [Tailscale](https://tailscale.com/) (`ts.net` names)
:::

:::caution[A domain name is REQUIRED]
Bedrock Voice Chat does not work with a bare IP address. You **MUST** use a fully qualified domain name.
:::

BVC gets and renews its TLS certificate through ACME DNS-01 with Let's Encrypt. It supports two DNS providers: Cloudflare and acme-dns. You can also use your own certificate files. See [TLS certificates](/wiki/server/tls/).

:::tip[Cloudflare DNS]
Use Cloudflare if your domain is registered with Cloudflare or moved to Cloudflare. Cloudflare DNS is free.
:::

## Firewall configuration

Open these ports in the firewall.

| Port | Protocol | Purpose |
|------|----------|---------|
| 443 | TCP | HTTP API, WebSocket, and WebSocket voice when UDP is blocked. |
| 28280 | UDP | Voice traffic (QUIC). |
| 28284 | UDP | Peering with other BVC servers. Open it only if you use [peering](/wiki/reference/peering/). |

## Running Bedrock Voice Chat with Docker

Docker is the recommended method. You can also run the native server binary from [GitHub](https://github.com/Alaydriem/bedrock-voice-chat/releases).

1. Create `config.hcl`. This is the minimum configuration:

   ```hcl
   server {
       tls {
           names = ["replace.with.your.domain.name.tld"]

           acme {
               email    = "you@example.com"
               provider = "cloudflare"
               api_token = "${env.CF_API_TOKEN}"
           }
       }
   }
   ```

   All configuration keys are in the [configuration reference](/wiki/reference/configuration/).

2. Start the server with Docker:

   ```bash
   docker run -d --restart=always --name bvc \
     -p 443:443/tcp -p 28280:28280/udp -p 28284:28284/udp \
     -e CF_API_TOKEN="your_cloudflare_api_token" \
     -v ${PWD}:/data \
     ghcr.io/alaydriem/bedrock-voice-chat/server:1.0.0-beta.21
   ```

3. Get your access token:

   ```bash
   docker exec -it bvc bvc-server admin token mint --local -c /data/config.hcl
   ```

   :::caution[Save this token]
   The Bedrock Addon and the Java mod need this token.
   :::

4. Make yourself the first admin. The command creates your player record if it does not exist.

   ```bash
   docker exec -it bvc bvc-server admin bootstrap -p <YourGamertag>
   ```

5. Sign in to the Bedrock Voice Chat app.

## Next steps

1. Install the [Bedrock Addon](/wiki/server/bedrock-addon/) or the [Java mod](/wiki/server/java-mod/).
2. Let your players in. A player can sign in after they join your game server once, or after you [add them](/wiki/server/players-and-permissions/).
3. Send your players to [Downloads](/wiki/start/downloads/).

Realms, Aternos and consoles need more setup. See [Where BVC works](/wiki/platforms/).

## Embedded server in the Java mod

If you run a Geyser server with PaperMC or Fabric, the Java mod can run the BVC server inside the game server. See the [Java mod guide](/wiki/server/java-mod/).

---

# Java mod

> BVC on Fabric and PaperMC, in external or embedded mode.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/server/java-mod

Bedrock Voice Chat runs on Minecraft Java servers with a mod for Fabric and PaperMC. Download it from [Modrinth](https://modrinth.com/mod/bedrock-voice-chat). For crossplay with Bedrock players, use [Geyser and Floodgate](/wiki/server/java-mod/integrations/geyser-and-floodgate/).

## Loaders

| Loader | Directory | Configuration |
|---|---|---|
| [Fabric](/wiki/server/java-mod/fabric/) | `mods/` | JSON |
| [PaperMC](/wiki/server/java-mod/papermc/) | `plugins/` | YAML |

## Integrations

The mod detects other plugins and mods at startup. See [Integrations](/wiki/server/java-mod/integrations/) for [Geyser and Floodgate](/wiki/server/java-mod/integrations/geyser-and-floodgate/) and [Simple Voice Chat](/wiki/server/java-mod/integrations/simple-voice-chat/).

## External or embedded server

The mod connects to an external BVC server, or runs an embedded BVC server.

**External** mode connects to a standalone BVC server. Use external mode on most hosts. It gives better performance.
