**Embedded** mode runs BVC inside the game server's JVM. You do not run a separate service. Use it for small servers and local development. Some hosts, for example [Nodecraft](/wiki/platforms/nodecraft/), support embedded mode.

:::caution
Embedded mode needs a host that runs all the time and has enough memory. On low-end hosts, or hosts that suspend idle servers, audio quality and performance can be bad. These problems are difficult to trace. If you see them, move BVC to its own machine.
:::

## Support

Report problems with the mod on [GitHub](https://github.com/Alaydriem/bedrock-voice-chat/issues).

---

# Fabric

> Install and configure the BVC mod on a Fabric server.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/server/java-mod/fabric

The Bedrock Voice Chat Fabric mod reads its configuration from `config/bedrock-voice-chat.json`.

## Install

1. Put [fabric-api](https://modrinth.com/mod/fabric-api) in the server's `mods` directory.
2. Put `bedrock-voice-chat.jar` in `mods`.
3. Start the server once. The mod writes `config/bedrock-voice-chat.json`.
4. Stop the server, edit the file, and start the server again.

## External mode

The mod sends player positions to a standalone [BVC server](/wiki/server/installation/).

```json
{
  "bvc-server": "https://bvc.example.com",
  "access-token": "<server.minecraft.access_token from config.hcl>"
}
```

Both keys are required. `access-token` must be the same as `server.minecraft.access_token` in the BVC server's `config.hcl`. If the values are different, the BVC server rejects each position update.

## Embedded mode

The mod runs the BVC server inside the Minecraft server's JVM.

```json
{
  "use-embedded-server": true,
  "embedded-config": {
    "server": {
      "port": 8444,
      "quic_port": 8443,
      "tls": {
        "names": ["bvc.example.com"],
        "acme": {
          "email": "you@example.com",
          "provider": "cloudflare",
          "api_token": "<Cloudflare API token>"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Replace `bvc.example.com` with your domain. Set `api_token` to a Cloudflare API token with DNS edit permission on that zone. BVC gets and renews the TLS certificate automatically. See [TLS](/wiki/server/tls/) to make the token, or to use acme-dns or your own certificate files.

`embedded-config` uses the same keys and the same nesting as the BVC server's `config.hcl`. A key that is not set uses the server default. See the [configuration reference](/wiki/reference/configuration/) for all keys.

The mod keeps its certificate authority (the key that signs player certificates) in `config/bedrock-voice-chat/`. Back up this directory. If you delete it, all client certificates that the server issued become invalid.

:::note
Releases before 1.0.0-beta.21 used flat keys in `embedded-config`. [Upgrading to beta.21](/wiki/upgrading/beta-21/#java-mod) has the table of old keys and new keys.
:::

## Chat sync

To read and send in-game [chat](/wiki/player/chat/) from the BVC app, set this line in `server.properties`:

```properties
enforce-secure-profile=false
```

Restart the server after you change it.

## Next steps

1. Let your players in. A player can sign in after they join your game server once, or after you [add them](/wiki/server/players-and-permissions/).
2. Send your players to [Downloads](/wiki/start/downloads/).

---

# Integrations

> Other mods and plugins the BVC Java mod works with.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/server/java-mod/integrations

The Bedrock Voice Chat Java mod finds the mods and plugins below when the server starts. They are optional. Each page lists the BVC settings that the integration needs.

| Integration | Result | Configuration |
|---|---|---|
| [Geyser and Floodgate](/wiki/server/java-mod/integrations/geyser-and-floodgate/) | Bedrock players can join a Java server. BVC matches them to their Xbox gamertag. | None |
| [Simple Voice Chat](/wiki/server/java-mod/integrations/simple-voice-chat/) | Java players on Simple Voice Chat and BVC players hear each other. | Embedded mode: none. External mode: a peer link on each server. |

The mod looks for these integrations only at startup. If you add one later, restart the game server.

---

# Geyser and Floodgate

> BVC on Geyser and Floodgate cross-platform servers.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/server/java-mod/integrations/geyser-and-floodgate

Bedrock Voice Chat supports Geyser servers. Your Bedrock and Java players can hear each other in the same world. Install the [Java mod](/wiki/server/java-mod/) on Fabric or PaperMC, and configure it the same as on any Java server.

:::note
BVC needs no Geyser settings. Geyser shows Bedrock players to the Java server as Java players. The Java mod sends positions for all players in the same way.
:::

## Floodgate

When [Floodgate](https://geysermc.org/wiki/floodgate/) is on the classpath, Bedrock Voice Chat detects it at startup. You do not configure anything.

The mod matches each Floodgate player to their Xbox gamertag. It removes the Floodgate prefix character from the name. Bedrock players sign in to the BVC app with the gamertag that they use in game.

:::caution
Without Floodgate, the mod uses the Java username and logs:

```
Floodgate API not found on classpath — prefix-strip path disabled
```

Bedrock players must then sign in with their Java username, not their gamertag. Install Floodgate.
:::

## Setup

1. Install the Java mod for [Fabric](/wiki/server/java-mod/fabric/) or [PaperMC](/wiki/server/java-mod/papermc/).
2. Install Floodgate with Geyser.

## Server mode

External and embedded mode both work. Use external mode on a Geyser server. Crossplay servers often have more players, and embedded mode uses the same CPU as the game server. See [Java mod](/wiki/server/java-mod/#external-or-embedded-server) for the two modes.

## Players

All players need the BVC app, on Java and on Bedrock. Bedrock players on a console use the mobile app on their own phone or tablet. See [console and mobile](/wiki/platforms/console-and-mobile/).

---

# Simple Voice Chat

> Bridge Simple Voice Chat and Bedrock Voice Chat on one Minecraft server.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/server/java-mod/integrations/simple-voice-chat

Bedrock Voice Chat connects to [Simple Voice Chat](https://modrinth.com/plugin/simple-voice-chat) (SVC). Java players on Simple Voice Chat and players on the BVC app can then hear each other in the same world.

## Requirements

| Component | Where |
|---|---|
| Bedrock Voice Chat Java mod | Fabric or PaperMC. See [Java mod](/wiki/server/java-mod/). |
| Simple Voice Chat | [The server plugin or mod](https://modrinth.com/plugin/simple-voice-chat). |
| A BVC server | Embedded in the game server, or external. |

## Setup with an embedded server

When you use the embedded server, BVC configures the bridge automatically.

1. Install the BVC mod and Simple Voice Chat on your PaperMC or Fabric server.
2. Enable the embedded server. See [Fabric](/wiki/server/java-mod/fabric/#embedded-mode) or [PaperMC](/wiki/server/java-mod/papermc/#embedded-mode).

## Setup with an external server

With an external BVC server, connect the game server and the BVC server with peer links. A peer link is a code that lets two servers trust each other. Add the game server's peer link to the BVC server, and the BVC server's peer link to the game server.

1. Install the BVC mod and Simple Voice Chat on your PaperMC or Fabric server.
2. Configure the BVC mod to use an [external server](/wiki/server/java-mod/#external-or-embedded-server).
3. Start the game server. The console shows a `peers` block with the game server's peer link:

   ```
   peers "svc-bridge" {
     peerlink = "bvcpeer..."
   }
   ```

4. Add this block inside the `server` block of the BVC server's `config.hcl`. Restart the BVC server.

   ```hcl
   server {
      tls {}
      bedrock {}

      peers "svc-bridge" {
         peerlink = "bvcpeer..."
      }
   }
   ```

5. When the BVC server starts, it logs its own peer link:

   ```
   INFO bvc_server_lib::runtime: this server's peer link peerlink=bvcpeer....
   ```

   :::tip[Get the peer link]
   To show the peer link at any time, run:

   ```
   bvc-server relay peerlink
   ```
   :::

6. Set `svc-bridge-peerlink` to the BVC server's peer link in the mod configuration. This is `config/bedrock-voice-chat.json` on Fabric, or `plugins/BedrockVoiceChat/config.yml` on PaperMC. Restart the game server.

   ```
   svc-bridge-peerlink: "bvcpeer...the-link-from-the-bvc-server-log"
   ```

## Settings

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `svc-bridge-peerlink` | None | The BVC server's peer link. Required in external mode. Ignored in embedded mode. |

---

# PaperMC

> Install and configure the BVC plugin on a PaperMC server.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/server/java-mod/papermc

The Bedrock Voice Chat PaperMC plugin reads its configuration from `plugins/BedrockVoiceChat/config.yml`.

## Install

1. Put the plugin JAR in the server's `plugins` directory.
2. Start the server once. The plugin writes `plugins/BedrockVoiceChat/config.yml`, with comments.
3. Stop the server, edit the file, and start the server again.

## External mode

The plugin sends player positions to a standalone [BVC server](/wiki/server/installation/).

```yaml
bvc-server: "https://bvc.example.com"
access-token: "<server.minecraft.access_token from config.hcl>"
```

Both keys are required. `access-token` must be the same as `server.minecraft.access_token` in the BVC server's `config.hcl`. If the values are different, the BVC server rejects each position update.

## Embedded mode

The plugin runs the BVC server inside the Minecraft server's JVM.

```yaml
use-embedded-server: true
embedded-config:
  server:
    port: 8444
    quic_port: 8443
    tls:
      names:
        - "bvc.example.com"
      acme:
        email: "you@example.com"
        provider: "cloudflare"
        api_token: "<Cloudflare API token>"
```

Replace `bvc.example.com` with your domain. Set `api_token` to a Cloudflare API token with DNS edit permission on that zone. BVC gets and renews the TLS certificate automatically. See [TLS](/wiki/server/tls/) to make the token, or to use acme-dns or your own certificate files.

`embedded-config` uses the same keys and the same nesting as the BVC server's `config.hcl`. A key that is not set uses the server default. See the [configuration reference](/wiki/reference/configuration/) for all keys.

The plugin keeps its certificate authority (the key that signs player certificates) in `plugins/BedrockVoiceChat/`. Back up this directory. If you delete it, all client certificates that the server issued become invalid.

:::caution
Earlier Paper releases used `embedded:` for this block. The plugin ignores `embedded:`. Rename it to `embedded-config:`.

Releases before 1.0.0-beta.21 used flat keys in this block. [Upgrading to beta.21](/wiki/upgrading/beta-21/#java-mod) has the table of old keys and new keys.
:::

## Chat sync

To read and send in-game [chat](/wiki/player/chat/) from the BVC app, set this line in `server.properties`:

```properties
enforce-secure-profile=false
```

Restart the server after you change it.

## Next steps

1. Let your players in. A player can sign in after they join your game server once, or after you [add them](/wiki/server/players-and-permissions/).
2. Send your players to [Downloads](/wiki/start/downloads/).

---

# Monitoring

> Prometheus metrics, health endpoints, and logging.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/server/monitoring

Bedrock Voice Chat server has health endpoints, Prometheus metrics, and structured logs for monitoring a deployment.

## Health endpoints

| Endpoint | Use |
|---|---|
| `/health/liveness` | The process is running. Restart the container if this fails. |
| `/health/readiness` | The server can accept traffic. Use it for the load balancer check. |
| `/api/ping` | A light check that the server is reachable. |

These endpoints need no authentication. See [Docker](/wiki/server/docker/) for probe configuration.

## Metrics

`/metrics` serves Prometheus format. It is always on. The `telemetry` feature flag controls only the data that BVC sends to the BVC developers. It does not change `/metrics`.

```yaml
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: bvc
    scheme: https
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['example.bedrockvc.stream:443']
```

## Logging

```hcl
log {
    level = "info"
    path  = "./logs"
}
```

`level` is `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, or `error`. The default is `info`.

Use `debug` when connections open and then fail. At `debug`, the server logs QUIC path and handshake details. It writes many log lines. Set the level back to `info` when you are done.

The server always writes to both outputs:

- **stderr**: human-readable text with colour. Colour turns off when stderr is not a terminal.
- **`log.path`**: one JSON object per line. The file rotates at 50 MB, and the server keeps ten old files.

Send the JSON log file to your log system. Do not use the console output. Every line has `ts`, `level`, `target`, `msg`, `instance_id`, `name`, and `boot_id`. Some lines have more fields, as top-level keys.

```bash
jq -r 'select(.level=="warn" or .level=="error") | "\(.ts) \(.target) \(.msg)"' logs/bvc-server.log
```

`boot_id` changes each time the server starts. Use it to find the lines from one run in a file.

`RUST_LOG` overrides `level` and the default level of each module. It applies to the server and to its libraries:

```bash
RUST_LOG=info,bvc_server_lib::stream=debug,hyper=off
```

## What to watch

**Voice fails while HTTP works.** HTTP uses TCP/443. Voice uses QUIC on UDP/28280. If UDP is blocked, players can sign in but hear nothing, and HTTP checks still pass. Alert on the QUIC connection count.

**UDP reachability.** In most broken deployments, the UDP port is closed. Test it with a probe from outside your network. Do not rely on the firewall configuration.

**Certificate expiry**, if you supply your own certificates. BVC renews ACME certificates. It does not renew PEM files that you supply.

**Disk space**, if many players have `audio_upload`. The audio library has no limit for each player.

## Checking a deployment from outside

```bash
curl https://example.bedrockvc.stream/api/config
```

A JSON response shows that HTTP, TLS and TCP/443 work. It does not show that voice works. Voice uses QUIC over UDP, and a closed UDP port is the most common fault. Test voice with a real client.

---

# No-net Addon

> Build and install the Addon for Realms, Aternos, and hosts without @minecraft/server-net.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/server/nonet-addon

The no-net Addon lets Bedrock Voice Chat run on hosts that do not allow `@minecraft/server-net`, such as Realms and Aternos. Without that module, the standard Addon cannot send HTTP requests. It cannot send positions to the BVC server.

With the no-net Addon, the BVC app runs a local Bedrock server. Minecraft connects to this local server. The app sends all game traffic to the real host, and reads player positions from that traffic.

For host-specific steps, see [Realms](/wiki/platforms/realms/) and [Aternos](/wiki/platforms/aternos/).

## Before you start

Install and configure the [BVC server](/wiki/server/installation/) first.

:::caution
The no-net Addon needs a Bedrock Voice Chat server.
:::

Install the [BVC app](/wiki/start/downloads/). You use the app to connect to the host.

## Limitations

- The Addon is **locked to one protocol version**. An Addon for one Bedrock version does not work with a different version.
- Support for each Minecraft release comes after the release. Mojang does not document the packet protocol and changes it in each update. The BVC developers cannot update the Addon until the Minecraft update is released.
- If your host updates Minecraft automatically, voice chat stops on the day of the update.
- Your host's Minecraft version must match the version that the Addon supports. If the versions do not match, voice chat does not work. Check [version support](/wiki/platforms/version-support/) before you choose a server version.

These limits do not apply to your own Bedrock Dedicated Server with the [full Addon](/wiki/server/bedrock-addon/).

## Build the world

1. Download `no-net.mcaddon` from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Alaydriem/bedrock-voice-chat/releases) (releases with a tag that starts with `mods-`), or from CurseForge. Use the `no-net` variant. The full Addon does not work on these hosts.

2. Double-click the file to install it in your Minecraft Bedrock client.

3. Create a new world. Under **Behavior Packs**, enable the **Bedrock Voice Chat (Realms + No-Net Servers)** pack.

   <div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/mc-packs-active.jpg" alt="Pack list with the Bedrock Voice Chat (Realms + No-Net Servers) pack active" /></div>

4. Under **Experiments**, enable **Beta APIs**.

   <div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/mc-experiments.jpg" alt="Experiments toggle showing Beta APIs enabled" /></div>

5. Create the world, then exit it immediately.

6. Open the world's settings and export the world. Save the `.mcworld` file where you can find it again.

   <div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/mc-export-world.jpg" alt="World settings with the Export World option at the bottom" /></div>

## Upload and connect

Upload the world to your host. Then connect the BVC app to the host with Bedrock Voice Chat Connect. The upload step is different for each host:

- **[Realms](/wiki/platforms/realms/)**: upload the world to the Realm.
- **[Aternos and other no-net hosts](/wiki/platforms/aternos/)**: rename the file to `.zip`, then upload it.

## Console players

Console players need no extra steps. The BVC app shows the world on your local network, and Minecraft lists it under **Worlds**. See [console and mobile](/wiki/platforms/console-and-mobile/).

## Chat

[Chat](/wiki/player/chat/) needs no configuration on a no-net host. The BVC app reads chat from the game traffic, in the same way as positions. The app can read and send in-game chat after you connect.

The `bvc_world_name` variable of the [full Addon](/wiki/server/bedrock-addon/) does not apply to the no-net Addon.

---

# Players and permissions

> Whitelisting, the three permissions, and bootstrapping your first admin.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/server/players-and-permissions

Bedrock Voice Chat lets a player sign in only when the server knows that player. The server knows a player in one of two ways:

1. The player joins your game server. The Bedrock Addon or the Java mod sends the player to BVC.
2. An admin adds the player in the app or with the CLI.

:::caution
A player who has not joined your game server and has not been added cannot sign in. The app shows `AUTH02`.
:::

The `bvc` commands below are the server executable, run as a command-line tool. See the [CLI reference](/wiki/reference/cli/).

## Bootstrapping the first admin

A new deployment has no admin. The commands that create the first admin write to the database directly. They do not use the HTTP API. Run them on the server host, in the directory that contains `config.hcl`.

```bash
# On the server host
bvc admin generate-code -p Alice -g minecraft -d 3600
# -> Code: ABCD1234

# Anywhere with network access
bvc login --code ABCD1234

# Back on the server host
bvc admin bootstrap -p Alice -g minecraft
```

`admin generate-code` and `admin bootstrap` both create the player record if it does not exist. You can use them on an empty database. `admin bootstrap` gives the player admin.

To check the result, run:

```bash
bvc whoami
```

The output shows the active identity, the server URL, the certificate expiry, and the effective permissions. `admin` must be in the list.

### On an embedded Java server

A Fabric or PaperMC server that runs the [embedded server](/wiki/server/java-mod/#external-or-embedded-server) has no `bvc` executable. Run this command from the game server console:

```
/bvc admin grant <Gamertag>
```

Use the Xbox gamertag that the player signs in with. The command creates the player record if it does not exist. The player can then sign in. See [Java commands](/wiki/player/in-game-commands/java/#admin).

## Adding players

After you have an admin identity, you can run the remaining commands from any computer. They connect to the server's HTTPS API with your client certificate (mTLS).

```bash
bvc user add -p Bob -g minecraft
bvc user generate-code -p Bob -g minecraft
```

Give Bob the code. Bob uses the code with `bvc login`, or signs in through the app.

`user add` returns 409 if the player already exists. `user generate-code` returns 404 if the player does not exist. Run `user add` first.

A code expires after one hour by default. The maximum is 24 hours.

An admin can also add players from **Settings → Manage Players** in the app.

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/settings-manage-players.jpg" alt="Manage Players page listing the players who can sign in to the server" /></div>

## Removing players

```bash
bvc user banish -p Bob -g minecraft
bvc user banish -p Bob -g minecraft --banish false
```

Banishing revokes the player's certificate and closes their voice session. If the player is connected, BVC disconnects them immediately.

You can reverse a banish. The player record stays. The CLI cannot delete a player record.

Unbanishing does not restore the revoked certificate. The player signs in again and gets a new certificate.

## Permissions

| Permission | Grants |
|---|---|
| `audio_upload` | Upload clips to the [audio library](/wiki/player/audio-library/). |
| `audio_delete` | Delete clips. |
| `admin` | Manage players and permissions. |

Peering is not a player permission. You declare a peer in [`server.peers`](/wiki/reference/configuration/#serverpeers). See [peering](/wiki/reference/peering/).

### Server-wide defaults

```hcl
permissions {
    defaults = {
        audio_upload = true
        audio_delete = false
        admin        = false
    }
}
```

### Per-player overrides

```bash
bvc permission allow -p Bob -g minecraft --permission audio_upload
bvc permission deny  -p Bob -g minecraft --permission audio_upload
bvc permission clear -p Bob -g minecraft --permission audio_upload
bvc permission list  -p Bob -g minecraft
```

`allow` and `deny` set an override for one player. `clear` removes the override. The default from `config.hcl` then applies again.

If `list` prints nothing, the player has no overrides. Only the defaults apply.

In the app, **Manage Players** sets the same three overrides. Click the settings icon on the player's row. **Default** removes the override.

On an embedded Java server, use `/bvc admin grant`, `revoke` and `deny` in the console to set the `admin` override. `revoke` does the same as `clear`. See [Java commands](/wiki/player/in-game-commands/java/#admin).

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/settings-manage-permissions.jpg" alt="Permissions dialog for a player with Default, Allow, and Deny for Administrator, Upload sounds, and Delete sounds" /></div>

## Recommended defaults

On a public server, set `audio_upload` to `false` by default. Give it to players you trust. Uploaded clips use disk space on your server, and there is no limit for each player.

On a private server, keep the defaults.

---

# Privacy and telemetry

> What BVC collects, how to turn it off, and setting a minimum age for your community.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/server/privacy-and-telemetry

Bedrock Voice Chat collects a small amount of anonymous telemetry. You can turn it off.

## Telemetry

Bedrock Voice Chat collects anonymous operational metrics: connection counts, session start and end events, and error rates.

It does not collect gamertags, message content, audio, or position data.

Telemetry is on by default. To turn it off:

```hcl
server {
    features {
        telemetry = false
    }
}
```

You can also set `BVC_TELEMETRY=false`.

Turning telemetry off does not change how BVC works. The BVC developers then cannot see crashes and regressions on your server.

## Your own metrics

`/metrics` always serves Prometheus metrics, whatever the value of the `telemetry` flag. The health endpoints are always available. BVC does not send these metrics to anyone. Only your own deployment can read them.

See [monitoring](/wiki/server/monitoring/).

## Minimum age

Set a minimum age with `server.age.minimum`. In regions that require age checks, the client app then asks the player to confirm their age. Android uses Age Signals. iOS uses Declared Age Ranges.

```hcl
server {
    age {
        minimum = 13
    }
}
```

| Value | Effect |
|---|---|
| `0` | No age check. |
| `13` to `18` | Players must be at least this age. |
| Any other value | Changed to the nearest value from 13 to 18. |
| Not set | 13. |

The prompt appears only if the minimum is not `0` and the platform requires age checks in the player's region. Players in other regions see no change.

BVC asks the platform only if the signed-in player is at or above your minimum age. BVC does not receive, store, or send any player's age.

[Parents and age settings](/wiki/player/parents-and-age/) explains these settings for parents. If your server has younger players, link that page from your server rules.

## Player-to-player controls

Players can mute each other on their own device. When you mute a player, you do not hear them. They can still hear you.

BVC has no server-side moderation tools for voice. To remove a player from voice chat, use `bvc user banish`. For other moderation, use your community rules and moderators.

Group members can hear everything in the group. Any member can record the group on their own device.

## Full privacy policy

[PRIVACY_STATEMENT.md](https://github.com/Alaydriem/bedrock-voice-chat/blob/master/PRIVACY_STATEMENT.md)

---

# TLS certificates

> An assigned hostname, automatic certificates over ACME DNS-01, or bring your own.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/server/tls

Bedrock Voice Chat requires a valid TLS certificate. The client apps check it the same way a browser does.

:::danger
Self-signed certificates **will not work**. The app refuses the connection, and you cannot turn this check off.
:::

There are three options. Use only one. If you configure more than one, the server does not start.

| Option | When to use |
|---|---|
| **An assigned hostname** | You have no domain. BVC gives you a name and renews its certificate. In development, and available only to some Patreon and YouTube members. See [assigned hostnames](/wiki/server/enrollment/). |
| **ACME** | You have a domain and a supported DNS provider. BVC gets and renews the certificate. |
| **Your own PEM files** | You already have a certificate, or your DNS provider is not supported. |

## ACME

BVC uses a DNS record to prove that you control the domain (ACME DNS-01). You do not need to open port 80 or run an HTTP service. Renewal is automatic.

BVC supports two DNS providers.

### Cloudflare

```hcl
server {
    tls {
        names = ["example.bedrockvc.stream"]

        acme {
            email     = "you@example.com"
            provider  = "cloudflare"
            api_token = "${env.CF_API_TOKEN}"
        }
    }
}
```

:::caution[Use a scoped API token]
Create an API token on Cloudflare's **API Tokens** page. Limit it to one zone, with **DNS edit** permission. Do not use the global API key. It gives BVC control of your whole Cloudflare account.
:::

### acme-dns

Use acme-dns when your DNS provider has no supported API, or when you do not want to give BVC credentials for your main DNS zone.

Add a CNAME that points your `_acme-challenge` record to the acme-dns server. BVC writes only to the acme-dns server. It does not change your DNS zone.

```hcl
server {
    tls {
        names = ["example.bedrockvc.stream"]

        acme {
            email      = "you@example.com"
            provider   = "acme-dns"
            server_url = "https://auth.acme-dns.io"
            username   = "${env.ACME_DNS_USERNAME}"
            password   = "${env.ACME_DNS_PASSWORD}"
            subdomain  = "${env.ACME_DNS_SUBDOMAIN}"
        }
    }
}
```

Register with the acme-dns server first. Registration gives you the username, the password, the subdomain, and the CNAME to add.

## Your own certificate

```hcl
server {
    tls {
        names       = ["example.bedrockvc.stream"]
        certificate = "/etc/bvc/fullchain.pem"
        key         = "/etc/bvc/privkey.pem"
    }
}
```

:::caution[Use the full chain]
Use `fullchain.pem`. A certificate without the intermediate certificate works on a computer that already has the intermediate cached. It fails on a new phone.
:::

If you use your own certificate files, replace them before they expire.

---

# Troubleshooting

> Diagnosing a BVC deployment from the operator side.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/server/troubleshooting

Check a Bedrock Voice Chat deployment from the outside in. Do the checks in order.

## 1. Server reachability

```bash
curl https://example.bedrockvc.stream/api/config
```

If the response is JSON, the process is running, TLS is valid, and TCP/443 is open.

If the response is not JSON, the problem is in the server, its network, or its certificate.

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| Connection refused | The server is not running, or the port is not published. |
| Timeout | Firewall or port forwarding. |
| Certificate error | See [TLS](/wiki/server/tls/). A self-signed certificate does not work. |
| 404 | A different service is listening on that address. |

## 2. UDP port

HTTP uses TCP/443. Voice uses QUIC on UDP/28280. If TCP/443 is open and UDP/28280 is closed, sign-in works and HTTP checks pass, but nobody hears audio.

Make sure that UDP/28280 is published and reachable. Test it separately from TCP. In Docker, publish `-p 28280:28280/udp`.

When a client's network blocks UDP, the client sends voice over WebSocket on TCP/443.

## 3. Addon position updates

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <your token>" https://example.bedrockvc.stream/api/position
```

If the response lists players, the game server, the Addon and BVC all work. If the list is empty, the game server does not send positions.

For BDS, set `content-log-console-output-enabled=true`. When the world loads, look for `[BVC] Connecting to:`. If the line is missing, the Addon is not running. Check Beta APIs, the world's pack list, and `permissions.json`.

The most common cause of an empty list is an `access_token` in the Addon that does not match `config.hcl`. BVC rejects each of these position updates without an error.

## 4. Whitelist

```bash
bvc whoami
bvc permission list -p <player> -g minecraft
```

A player can sign in only after they join your game server once, or after an admin adds them. See [players and permissions](/wiki/server/players-and-permissions/).

## Specific symptoms

**Sign-in works, but there is no audio.** The cause is usually a closed UDP port. Go back to step 2.

**Audio works for some players and not for others.** The networks of those players probably block UDP. Make sure that TCP/443 is open for the WebSocket fallback.

**Everything worked, then stopped after a Minecraft update.** This affects only Realms and Aternos. See [version support](/wiki/platforms/version-support/).

**Console players cannot connect.** The console and the device that runs BVC must be on the same network. In Minecraft, the session shows on the Worlds tab, not the Servers tab. See [console and mobile](/wiki/platforms/console-and-mobile/).

**All players were signed out at the same time.** The database that holds the mTLS certificate authority was lost or replaced. All client certificates are now invalid, and every player must sign in again. If you have a backup of the database, restore it.

**Audio gets worse as more players join.** The server needs more CPU. Add cores. Embedded mode on a shared host often causes this. Move BVC to its own machine.

**A player connects, then goes silent after a few minutes, again and again.** This usually happens on mobile data or behind carrier-grade NAT. The carrier closes the idle UDP mapping, and the player's device reconnects from a new port. QUIC permits only a few port changes for each connection. After that limit, the connection stays open but sends no audio.

The server sends a keepalive every 10 seconds. This is shorter than the carrier timeouts that are known. You cannot change the interval. If the problem continues, record the player's network type and open an issue.

## Debug logging

```hcl
log {
    level = "debug"
}
```

At `debug`, the server logs QUIC path and handshake details. Use it when connections open and then fail. The server writes many lines at this level. Set the level back to `info` when you are done.

## Reporting a problem

Include:

- The output of `/api/config`.
- Whether UDP/28280 is open.
- Whether `/api/position` returns data.
- How you run the server (Docker, bare metal, or embedded).
- What you already checked.

Report on [Discord](https://discord.gg/CdtchD5zxr) or open a [GitHub issue](https://github.com/Alaydriem/bedrock-voice-chat/issues).

---

# Where BVC works

> Compatibility across Bedrock Dedicated Server, Java, Realms, Aternos, Geyser, consoles, and LAN.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/platforms

Bedrock Voice Chat works on every Minecraft server where you can install an Addon or a mod.

:::caution
Worlds that the Minecraft game client hosts are **not** supported. These are LAN worlds, locally hosted worlds, and single-player worlds. See [LAN and local worlds](/wiki/platforms/lan-and-local-worlds/).
:::

## Compatibility

| Setup | Supported | Requirements |
|---|---|---|
| **Bedrock Dedicated Server** | Yes | The [Addon](/wiki/server/bedrock-addon/). No delay after Minecraft updates. |
| **Java: Fabric or Paper** | Yes | The [Java mod](/wiki/server/java-mod/), external or embedded. |
| **Geyser / Floodgate** | Yes | The Java mod. The mod detects Floodgate automatically. No BVC settings for Geyser. [Details](/wiki/server/java-mod/integrations/geyser-and-floodgate/). |
| **Realms** | Yes | The [no-net Addon](/wiki/server/nonet-addon/) and Bedrock Voice Chat Connect in the app. [Details](/wiki/platforms/realms/). |
| **Nodecraft** | Yes | A Pro server. [Details](/wiki/platforms/nodecraft/). |
| **Aternos and other no-net hosts** | Yes | The no-net Addon and Bedrock Voice Chat Connect. [Details](/wiki/platforms/aternos/). |
| **Consoles** | Yes | The mobile app on a phone or tablet. [Details](/wiki/platforms/console-and-mobile/). |
| **LAN worlds** | No | There is no server to install the Addon on. See [LAN and local worlds](/wiki/platforms/lan-and-local-worlds/). |
| **Locally hosted / single-player worlds** | No | There is no server to install the Addon on. See [LAN and local worlds](/wiki/platforms/lan-and-local-worlds/). |

See [version support](/wiki/platforms/version-support/) for the Bedrock versions that BVC supports on Realms and Aternos.

---

# Aternos and no-net hosts

> Run BVC on Aternos and other hosts that cannot enable @minecraft/server-net.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/platforms/aternos

Bedrock Voice Chat supports Aternos and other free hosts that do not allow `@minecraft/server-net`. Use the no-net Addon and Bedrock Voice Chat Connect. Supported since 1.0.0-beta.15.

The BVC app runs a local Bedrock server. Minecraft connects to the app, and the app connects to Aternos.

:::caution
Support for each Minecraft release comes after the release. If your host updates Minecraft automatically, voice chat **stops** on the day of the update. Check [version support](/wiki/platforms/version-support/) before you move your server to Aternos.
:::

## Before you start

1. Install and configure the [BVC server](/wiki/server/installation/).
2. Install the [BVC app](/wiki/start/downloads/).
3. Build the no-net world with the [no-net Addon](/wiki/server/nonet-addon/) guide.

## Upload the world

1. Find the `.mcworld` file that you exported, and change the extension to `.zip`.
2. Upload it to Aternos.

   <div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/aternos-worlds.jpg" alt="Aternos world upload page" /></div>

3. Set the Aternos server version to the Minecraft version that the Addon supports. Each Addon works with one Minecraft version only. If the versions do not match, voice chat does not work.

Check [version support](/wiki/platforms/version-support/) for the version to select.

## Connect

1. Sign in to the BVC app with the BVC server from [Before you start](#before-you-start).
2. Select the Settings cog at the bottom left. Then select **Voice Chat Connect** in the sidebar. The first time, the app asks you to sign in again.
3. Select the add button at the top. Enter your Aternos domain and port.

   <div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/settings-connect-aternos-edit.jpg" alt="Bedrock Voice Chat Connect add-server dialog with an Aternos address" /></div>

4. Select **Connect**. The app shows the connection details.

   <div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/settings-connect-aternos-connected.jpg" alt="Bedrock Voice Chat Connect showing connection information for a connected server" /></div>

## Open Minecraft

The BVC app shows the session on your local network. Minecraft lists it under **Worlds**.

1. Open Minecraft on the same network as the device that runs BVC.
2. Go to **Worlds**.
3. Select the entry with the name of your server. The second line shows your gamertag and **Bedrock Voice Chat**.

Desktop, mobile and console all connect this way. Consoles need no extra setup. See [console and mobile](/wiki/platforms/console-and-mobile/).

:::danger
Join the world from the **Worlds** tab. If you connect to your Aternos server directly, Minecraft works but voice chat does not.
:::

:::note
On desktop and mobile, if the session is not in **Worlds**, open the **Servers** tab and add `127.0.0.1` with port `28282`.
:::

---

# Console and mobile

> Using BVC on Xbox, PlayStation, Switch, and mobile devices.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/platforms/console-and-mobile

Bedrock Voice Chat supports Xbox, PlayStation and Switch players with the mobile app. Your phone or tablet is your microphone and speaker. Use it next to the console.

You do not install anything on the console. BVC gets your position from the Minecraft server.

:::note
There is no Bedrock Voice Chat app for consoles. Consoles do not allow this type of app.

To help fund a console app, support Bedrock Voice Chat on Patreon or as a YouTube member.
:::

## Get the app

- **Android**: [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.alaydriem.bvc.client), open beta.
- **iOS / iPadOS**: [TestFlight](https://testflight.apple.com/join/JSG7bVqC).

Sign in with the Xbox account that you play on.

## On a Bedrock Dedicated Server

No extra steps. Join the server in Minecraft and sign in to the app.

## On Realms or Aternos

Realms and Aternos use Bedrock Voice Chat Connect. The BVC app shows the session on your local network, and Minecraft lists it under **Worlds**.

### Operator

Operators do not need to change any settings.

### Player

1. Connect the console and the phone that runs BVC to the same network.
2. Open BVC. Open **Settings**, then **Voice Chat Connect**.
3. Select your Realm or server. Wait for the connection details.
4. Open Minecraft on the console. Go to **Worlds**.
5. Select the entry with the name of your world. The second line shows your gamertag and **Bedrock Voice Chat**.

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/mc-worlds.jpg" alt="Minecraft's Worlds tab showing a BVC session, world name on the first line and gamertag on the second" /></div>

If two people on the network run BVC in the same world, two entries show. Use the gamertag on the second line to find your entry.

:::danger
Do **not** enter your Realm or Aternos address directly. If you do, Minecraft works but voice chat does not.
:::

## Playing on mobile

If you play Minecraft on a phone or tablet, follow the steps on the [Realms](/wiki/platforms/realms/) and [Aternos](/wiki/platforms/aternos/) pages. They are the same as on desktop.

## Recording

:::note
Recording is not available on mobile. Record on a desktop computer. See [Recording](/wiki/creator/recording/).
:::

---

# LAN and local worlds

> Why BVC does not work on LAN, locally hosted, or single-player worlds.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/platforms/lan-and-local-worlds

Bedrock Voice Chat does not work on LAN worlds, locally hosted worlds or single-player worlds. These are worlds that one player hosts on their own device. Friends can join only while the host is online.

:::note[Two different things called LAN]
A **LAN world** is a world that a game client hosts. BVC does not support it.

Minecraft's **Worlds** tab also lists sessions that it finds on your network. Bedrock Voice Chat Connect sessions show in this list. These sessions work with BVC. See [Realms](/wiki/platforms/realms/) and [Aternos](/wiki/platforms/aternos/).
:::

## Reason

Bedrock Voice Chat needs an Addon on the server to send player positions. Proximity chat cannot work without positions, and only the Addon sends them.

A world that the Minecraft game client hosts cannot load server Addons. On all platforms, there is no place to install one.

### Bedrock Voice Chat Connect

Realms and Aternos use Bedrock Voice Chat Connect. Connect does not work with LAN worlds.

You can upload a world with the Addon to a Realm or an Aternos server. Connect then sends the data from that Addon to BVC. You cannot upload a world to a LAN host. No Addon runs on a LAN world.

## Use Bedrock Dedicated Server

Download Bedrock Dedicated Server (BDS) and start it. It can run on the computer that hosted the LAN world.

You need:

1. A **Bedrock Dedicated Server** or a **Java server**. See [Running a server](/wiki/server/).
2. The **BVC server**, on a host that players can reach.
3. The **BVC app** on the device of each player.

A local Bedrock Dedicated Server does not stop working after a Minecraft update. You choose when to update it.

## Future support

Every known solution needs code that runs on the world host. The Minecraft game client does not allow this.

To fund work on this problem, [support the project](/wiki/start/supporting-bvc/).

---

# Nodecraft

> Run Bedrock Voice Chat on a Nodecraft game server, for Fabric, PaperMC, and Bedrock.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/platforms/nodecraft

[Nodecraft](https://nodecraft.com/r/alaydriem) hosts Minecraft servers. Bedrock Voice Chat works on Nodecraft Java and Bedrock servers.

:::tip[Nodecraft discount]
Sign up through [nodecraft.com/r/alaydriem](https://nodecraft.com/r/alaydriem) to get the best discount. Sign-ups through this link also help fund Bedrock Voice Chat.
:::

## Requirements

- A Nodecraft server.
- A domain name. Bedrock Voice Chat does not work with an IP address or with the Nodecraft host name. See [TLS certificates](/wiki/server/tls/).
- A DNS provider that BVC can use to get a certificate. The guides use Cloudflare. See [TLS certificates](/wiki/server/tls/).

## Server type

| Server type | BVC server | Guide |
|---|---|---|
| **Fabric** | Embedded in the mod | [Fabric on Nodecraft](/wiki/platforms/nodecraft/fabric/) |
| **PaperMC** | Embedded in the plugin | [PaperMC on Nodecraft](/wiki/platforms/nodecraft/papermc/) |
| **Bedrock** | Started by the BVC launcher | [Bedrock on Nodecraft](/wiki/platforms/nodecraft/bedrock/) |

The Java guides use the [embedded mode](/wiki/server/java-mod/#external-or-embedded-server) of the mod. The BVC server runs inside the Minecraft server and uses the ports of the Nodecraft server.

## Support

For problems with the Nodecraft panel, billing, or the server itself, contact [Nodecraft support](https://nodecraft.com/support). For problems with Bedrock Voice Chat, see [server troubleshooting](/wiki/server/troubleshooting/) or [report an issue](/wiki/start/report-an-issue/).

---

# Bedrock on Nodecraft

> Run Bedrock Voice Chat and Bedrock Dedicated Server together on Nodecraft with the BVC launcher.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/platforms/nodecraft/bedrock

Install Bedrock Voice Chat on a Nodecraft Pro server that runs Minecraft: Bedrock Edition.

On Nodecraft, a custom launcher runs the Bedrock Voice Chat server next to your Bedrock Dedicated Server (BDS). When your Nodecraft Pro server starts, the launcher installs the Bedrock Voice Chat server and the BDS Addon, enables Beta APIs for your world, and sets up BDS.

## Before you start

You need:

- A Nodecraft Pro server. See [Nodecraft](/wiki/platforms/nodecraft/).
- A domain name, with DNS at Cloudflare or another [supported provider](/wiki/server/tls/).
- A Cloudflare API token for that zone, with DNS edit permission. See [TLS certificates](/wiki/server/tls/).

:::caution
You **MUST** use a Pro server. Lite servers stop when nobody plays. Bedrock Voice Chat then stops too.
:::

## Install Bedrock

1. Create a new **Pro** game server.
2. During server setup, select **Minecraft: Bedrock Edition**.
3. Select **Create and Deploy**. Wait for the installation to complete.

   <div class="shot"><span>Nodecraft game selection with Minecraft: Bedrock Edition</span></div>

## Upload the launcher

1. Download `bvc-launcher-linux-x64` from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Alaydriem/bedrock-voice-chat/releases).
2. In **Server Files** > **File Manager**, rename `bedrock_server` to `bedrock_server_vanilla`.
3. Select **Upload**, and upload `bvc-launcher-linux-x64` to the same directory. Rename it to `bedrock_server`.

   <div class="shot"><span>Nodecraft File Manager with bedrock_server and bedrock_server_vanilla</span></div>

4. Create `config/bvc.hcl` with this base configuration:

   ```hcl
   server {
       port = 28280
       quic_port = 28280

       tls {
           names = ["bvc.example.com"]

           acme {
               email = "your-cloudflare-email@example.com"
               provider = "cloudflare"
               api_token = "cfut_api-token"
           }
       }
   }
   ```

5. Replace `bvc.example.com`, the email, and the API token with your values.

:::caution
1. Use Cloudflare or another supported DNS provider. BVC then gets and renews the TLS certificate automatically.
2. Do not use your Nodecraft hostname. At this time, BVC cannot get a TLS certificate for the hostname that Nodecraft gives a Pro server.
3. Keep both ports at 28280. Do not change them.
:::

## Point your domain at the server

1. In the Pro Panel, select **Overview**. Copy the **Dedicated IP**.
2. At your DNS provider, add an `A` record for your BVC name, for example `bvc.example.com`, with the Dedicated IP as its value.
3. In Cloudflare, set the record's proxy status to **DNS only**.

BVC gets the TLS certificate the first time it starts. This can take one minute. Wait, then sign in for the first time.

:::caution
The launcher stores its certificate authority (the key that signs player certificates) in `bvc/`. Download a copy of this directory from **Server Files** and keep it. If you delete it, all client certificates that the server issued become invalid, and all players must sign in again.
:::

## Allowlist

Players in `allowlist.json` can sign in to Bedrock Voice Chat before they join the world for the first time. Other players can sign in after they join the world one time. If you remove a player from `allowlist.json`, they can still sign in to Bedrock Voice Chat.

## Connect

Your players sign in with `https://bvc.example.com:28280`. Use your domain. See [signing in](/wiki/player/signing-in/).

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/nodecraft-login.jpg" alt="BVC login window with bvc.example.com:28280 in the server address field" /></div>

## Next steps

1. Make yourself an admin from the server console:

   ```
   bvc admin grant <Gamertag>
   ```

   Use your Xbox gamertag, without quotes. To remove admin, run `bvc admin revoke <Gamertag>`.

2. Send your players to [Downloads](/wiki/start/downloads/). They can then sign in.

---

# Fabric on Nodecraft

> Run Bedrock Voice Chat on a Nodecraft Fabric server with the embedded BVC server.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/platforms/nodecraft/fabric

Install Bedrock Voice Chat on a Nodecraft Pro server that runs Fabric. The BVC server runs inside the Minecraft server (embedded mode). For the full list of mod settings, see [Fabric](/wiki/server/java-mod/fabric/).

## Before you start

You need:

- A Nodecraft Pro server. See [Nodecraft](/wiki/platforms/nodecraft/).
- A domain name, with DNS at Cloudflare or another [supported provider](/wiki/server/tls/).
- A Cloudflare API token for that zone, with DNS edit permission. See [TLS certificates](/wiki/server/tls/).

:::caution
You **MUST** use a Pro server. Lite servers stop when nobody plays. Bedrock Voice Chat then stops too.
:::

## Install Fabric

1. Create a new **Pro** game server.
2. During server setup, add a mod for **Fabric**.
3. Select **Create and Deploy**. Wait for the installation to complete.

   <div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/nodecraft-install-fabric.jpg" alt="Nodecraft Browse Mod to Install dialog filtered to Fabric" /></div>

## Upload the mods

1. Download [fabric-api](https://modrinth.com/mod/fabric-api) and [Bedrock Voice Chat](https://modrinth.com/mod/bedrock-voice-chat) from Modrinth. Select the Fabric versions that match your Minecraft version. To let Bedrock players join, also download the Fabric versions of Geyser and Floodgate. To connect players who use Simple Voice Chat, also download Simple Voice Chat.
2. In **Server Files** > **File Manager**, open the `mods` directory.
3. Select **Upload**, and upload all the `.jar` files.

   <div class="shot"><span>Nodecraft File Manager, mods directory with the BVC jar</span></div>

4. Create `config/bedrock-voice-chat.json` with this base configuration:

   ```json
   {
     "minimum-players": 1,
     "use-embedded-server": true,
     "embedded-config": {
       "server": {
         "port": 28280,
         "quic_port": 28280,
         "tls": {
           "names": ["bvc.example.com"],
           "ips": [],
           "acme": {
             "email": "your-cloudflare-email@example.com",
             "provider": "cloudflare",
             "api_token": "cfut_api-token"
           }
         }
       }
     }
   }
   ```

5. Replace `bvc.example.com`, the email, and the API token with your values.

:::caution
1. Use Cloudflare or another supported DNS provider. BVC then gets and renews the TLS certificate automatically.
2. Do not use your Nodecraft hostname. At this time, BVC cannot get a TLS certificate for the hostname that Nodecraft gives a Pro server.
3. Keep both ports at 28280. Do not change them.
:::

## Point your domain at the server

1. In the Pro Panel, select **Overview**. Copy the **Dedicated IP**.
2. At your DNS provider, add an `A` record for your BVC name, for example `bvc.example.com`, with the Dedicated IP as its value.
3. In Cloudflare, set the record's proxy status to **DNS only**.

BVC gets the TLS certificate the first time it starts. This can take one minute. Wait, then sign in for the first time. If players cannot sign in after BVC gets its first certificate, restart the Java server.

:::caution
The mod stores its certificate authority (the key that signs player certificates) in `config/bedrock-voice-chat/`. Download a copy of this directory from **Server Files** and keep it. If you delete it, all client certificates that the server issued become invalid, and all players must sign in again.
:::

## Chat sync

To read and send in-game chat from the BVC app, set this line in `server.properties`:

```properties
enforce-secure-profile=false
```

Edit `server.properties` in **Server Files**, then restart the server. See [chat](/wiki/player/chat/).

## Connect

Your players sign in with `https://bvc.example.com:28280`. Use your domain. See [signing in](/wiki/player/signing-in/).

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/nodecraft-login.jpg" alt="BVC login window with bvc.example.com:28280 in the server address field" /></div>

## Next steps

1. Make yourself an admin from the server console:

   ```
   /bvc admin grant <Gamertag>
   ```

   Use your Xbox gamertag. Put it in quotes if it contains a space. See [Java commands](/wiki/player/in-game-commands/java/#admin).

2. Send your players to [Downloads](/wiki/start/downloads/). They can then sign in.

---

# PaperMC on Nodecraft

> Run Bedrock Voice Chat on a Nodecraft PaperMC server with the embedded BVC server.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/platforms/nodecraft/papermc

Install Bedrock Voice Chat on a Nodecraft Pro server that runs PaperMC. The BVC server runs inside the Minecraft server (embedded mode). For the full list of plugin settings, see [PaperMC](/wiki/server/java-mod/papermc/).

## Before you start

You need:

- A Nodecraft Pro server. See [Nodecraft](/wiki/platforms/nodecraft/).
- A domain name, with DNS at Cloudflare or another [supported provider](/wiki/server/tls/).
- A Cloudflare API token for that zone, with DNS edit permission. See [TLS certificates](/wiki/server/tls/).

:::caution
You **MUST** use a Pro server. Lite servers stop when nobody plays. Bedrock Voice Chat then stops too.
:::

## Install Paper

1. Create a new **Pro** game server.
2. During server setup, add a mod for **Paper**.
3. Select **Create and Deploy**. Wait for the installation to complete.

   <div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/nodecraft-install-paper.jpg" alt="Nodecraft Browse Mod to Install dialog filtered to Paper" /></div>

## Upload the plugin

1. Download [Bedrock Voice Chat](https://modrinth.com/mod/bedrock-voice-chat) from Modrinth. Select the Paper version that matches your Minecraft version. To let Bedrock players join, also download Geyser and Floodgate. To connect players who use Simple Voice Chat, also download Simple Voice Chat.

   <div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/nodecraft-paper-plugins.jpg" alt="Nodecraft File Manager showing the plugins directory with the Bedrock Voice Chat, Geyser, Floodgate, and Simple Voice Chat jars" /></div>

4. Create `plugins/BedrockVoiceChat/config.yml` with this base configuration:

   ```yaml
   minimum-players: 1
   use-embedded-server: true
   embedded-config:
     server:
       port: 28280
       quic_port: 28280
       tls:
         names:
           - "bvc.example.com"
         ips: []
         acme:
           email: "your-cloudflare-email@example.com"
           provider: "cloudflare"
           api_token: "cfut_api-token"
   ```

5. Replace `bvc.example.com`, the email, and the API token with your values.

:::caution
1. Use Cloudflare or another supported DNS provider. BVC then gets and renews the TLS certificate automatically.

3. Keep both ports at 28280. Do not change them.
:::

## Point your domain at the server

1. In the Pro Panel, select **Overview**. Copy the **Dedicated IP**.
2. At your DNS provider, add an `A` record for your BVC name, for example `bvc.example.com`, with the Dedicated IP as its value.
3. In Cloudflare, set the record's proxy status to **DNS only**.

BVC gets the TLS certificate the first time it starts. This can take one minute. Wait, then sign in for the first time. If players cannot sign in after BVC gets its first certificate, restart the Java server.

:::caution
The plugin stores its certificate authority (the key that signs player certificates) in `plugins/BedrockVoiceChat/`. Download a copy of this directory from **Server Files** and keep it. If you delete it, all client certificates that the server issued become invalid, and all players must sign in again.
:::

## Chat sync

To read and send in-game chat from the BVC app, set this line in `server.properties`:

```properties
enforce-secure-profile=false
```

Edit `server.properties` in **Server Files**, then restart the server. See [chat](/wiki/player/chat/).

## Connect

Your players sign in with `https://bvc.example.com:28280`. Use your domain. See [signing in](/wiki/player/signing-in/).

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/nodecraft-login.jpg" alt="BVC login window with bvc.example.com:28280 in the server address field" /></div>

## Next steps

1. Make yourself an admin from the server console:

   ```
   /bvc admin grant <Gamertag>
   ```

   Use your Xbox gamertag. Put it in quotes if it contains a space. See [Java commands](/wiki/player/in-game-commands/java/#admin).

# Realms

> Run BVC on a Minecraft Realm using the no-net Addon and Bedrock Voice Chat Connect.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/platforms/realms

Bedrock Voice Chat supports Minecraft Realms with the no-net Addon and Bedrock Voice Chat Connect. You can use proximity voice chat on a Realm that you do not control. Supported since 1.0.0-beta.15.

:::caution
Realms update automatically. After a Minecraft update, voice chat on your Realm **stops** until a matching Bedrock Voice Chat version is available. Check [version support](/wiki/platforms/version-support/) before you move your server to a Realm.
:::

## Before you start

1. Install and configure the [BVC server](/wiki/server/installation/). Realms also need a BVC server.
2. Install the [BVC app](/wiki/start/downloads/).
3. Build the no-net world with the [no-net Addon](/wiki/server/nonet-addon/) guide.
4. Add each Realm player on the BVC server. See [players and permissions](/wiki/server/players-and-permissions/).

## Upload to the Realm

1. In Minecraft, open the settings of your Realm.
2. Replace the Realm world with the world that you built.
3. When the Realm has saved the world, leave the Realm.

## Connect

:::note
If you disconnect from Bedrock Voice Chat Connect, wait about five minutes before you connect again. Realms use NetherNet, and NetherNet does not accept a new connection during this time.
:::

1. Sign in to the BVC app with the BVC server from [Before you start](#before-you-start).
2. Select the Settings cog at the bottom left. Then select **Voice Chat Connect** in the sidebar. The first time, the app asks you to sign in again.
3. Select your Realm.

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/settings-connect.jpg" alt="Voice Chat Connect page with a Realm selected" /></div>

## Open Minecraft

The BVC app shows the session on your local network. Minecraft lists it under **Worlds**.

1. Open Minecraft on the same network as the device that runs BVC.
2. Go to **Worlds**.
3. Select the entry with the name of your Realm. The second line shows your gamertag and **Bedrock Voice Chat**.

Desktop, mobile and console all connect this way. Consoles need no extra setup. See [console and mobile](/wiki/platforms/console-and-mobile/).

:::danger
Join the world from the **Worlds** tab. If you connect to your Realm directly, Minecraft works but voice chat does not.
:::

:::note
On desktop and mobile, if the session is not in **Worlds**, open the **Servers** tab and add `127.0.0.1` with port `28282`.
:::
