# Bedrock version support

> The Bedrock versions that Bedrock Voice Chat Connect supports, and why support comes after each release.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/platforms/version-support

Bedrock Voice Chat Connect uses the Bedrock network protocol. Connect works only with the protocol versions in the table below.

This applies to Realms, Aternos and other hosts that use the no-net Addon.

:::note
This does not apply to a Bedrock Dedicated Server or a Java server. On these servers, the Addon or the mod sends positions over HTTP, and the Bedrock protocol version has no effect.
:::

<!-- generated:version-table start -->

## Supported Bedrock versions

| Minecraft Bedrock | Protocol |
|---|---|
| 1.26.0 | `v924` |
| 1.26.12 | `v944` |
| 1.26.20 | `v975` |
| 1.26.30 | `v1001` |
| 1.26.40 | `v2168` |
| 1.26.45 | `v2169` |
| 1.26.50 | `v2192` |
| 1.26.50 | `v2193` |

**1.26.50 is the newest supported release.**

## Not supported

These protocols are recognised but this build has no codec for them. The
no-net Addon and Bedrock Voice Chat Connect will not work against a server running one.

| Minecraft Bedrock | Protocol |
|---|---|
| 1.16.201 | `v422` |
| 1.16.220 | `v431` |
| 1.19.30 | `v554` |
| 1.20.61 | `v649` |
| 1.21.50 | `v766` |
| 1.21.90 | `v786` |

<!-- generated:version-table end -->

## Release delay

Mojang does not document the Bedrock packet protocol. Nearly every Bedrock release changes the protocol. For each change, the BVC developers reverse-engineer the new protocol and update BVC. Then they release new apps through each app store.

- The no-net Addon is locked to one protocol version. An Addon for one Bedrock version does not work with a different version. Use the server version that matches the Addon that you installed.
- If your host updates Minecraft automatically, voice chat stops on the day of the update. It works again when a matching Bedrock Voice Chat version is available.

:::tip
On your own Bedrock Dedicated Server, these limits do not apply. You choose when to update, and the Addon sends positions over HTTP. A protocol change does not affect it.

Patreon supporters and YouTube members get early access to builds and packs. They usually get support for a new Bedrock version before the general release. See [supporting BVC](/wiki/start/supporting-bvc/).
:::

## Advertised version

Each server in the app's server list has an advertised version setting. It sets the protocol version that Bedrock Voice Chat Connect reports to Minecraft. The default, Auto, uses the version that the Realm or host reports. Keep Auto unless a server does not connect with it.

---

# Streaming & recording

> Multi-track recording, Stream Deck control, and the local WebSocket API.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/creator

Bedrock Voice Chat gives creators multi-track recording, Stream Deck control, and a local API for your own tools. Each player records to a separate track. You can fix the audio of one player in post-production and not change the other tracks.

| Page | Contents |
|---|---|
| [Recording](/wiki/creator/recording/) | Record a session and export a track for each player as BWAV or MP4/Opus. |
| [Stream Deck](/wiki/creator/stream-deck/) | Mute, deafen and record from an Elgato Stream Deck. |
| [OBS Overlay](/wiki/creator/obs-overlay/) | Show who you can hear, and who is talking, in OBS. |
| [WebSocket API](/wiki/creator/websocket-api/) | Use the same controls from your own tools. |

:::note
Recording is available only on desktop. Mobile devices cannot write multi-track audio to storage fast enough.
:::

---

# OBS Overlay

> Show who you can hear, and who is talking, as a Browser source in OBS.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/creator/obs-overlay

Bedrock Voice Chat provides an overlay for OBS. Add it as a Browser source to show viewers who you can hear and who is talking. The overlay has a transparent background. It shows a list of players and the BVC logo in the corners of the screen. By default, both are on the left side.

The overlay shows a square for each member of your group, and for each nearby player whose microphone is on.

## Add the source

1. In Bedrock Voice Chat, open **Settings → WebSocket server**.
2. Copy the **OBS overlay** URL.
3. In OBS, add a **Browser** source.
4. Paste the URL.
5. Set **Width** to `3840` and **Height** to `2160`.

## Options

Add these query parameters to the URL:

| Option | Default | Values | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `layout` | `rail` | `rail`, `bar`, `chips` | A vertical column, a horizontal row, or small pills. |
| `anchor` | `tl` | `tl`, `tr`, `bl`, `br` | The corner for the squares. |
| `mark` | `bl` | `tl`, `tr`, `bl`, `br`, `off` | The corner for the logo. |
| `pulse` | `0` | `0`, `1` | `0` shows the logo at full height. `1` makes the logo rise and fall with the loudest speaker. |
| `self` | `0` | `0`, `1` | Whether you are in the list. |
| `faces` | `1` | `0`, `1` | Whether to show gamerpics. `0` always shows a letter. |
| `sources` | `1` | `0`, `1` | Whether group members look different from nearby players. |
| `quiet` | `1` | `0`, `1` | Whether silent players keep a square. `0` shows only the players who are talking. |
| `sort` | `name` | `name`, `activity` | `name` keeps the squares in a fixed order. `activity` moves the player who is talking to the front. |

For example, a horizontal row in the bottom-right corner that shows only the players who are talking:

```
http://127.0.0.1:9595/overlay?key=YOURKEY&layout=bar&anchor=br&quiet=0
```

## Size

The overlay is drawn for a 3840 by 2160 source. It scales to any scene size. One source works for 1080p and 4K canvases.

Use 3840 by 2160 in OBS, also when you stream at 1080p. An overlay that OBS scales down is sharper than one that OBS scales up.

## Blank overlay

- **Check the key.** If the key is wrong, the page shows a message instead of the overlay. Open the URL in a normal browser to read the message.
- **Check the port.** If a different program uses the port, Bedrock Voice Chat uses a different port. The URL in **Settings → WebSocket server** always contains the port in use.
- **Check that Bedrock Voice Chat is running.** The overlay dims when the connection to the app stops. It connects again when the app starts.
- **Use the URL from Settings.** The overlay must load from `127.0.0.1`. A copy of the page on a website cannot connect to the app.

---

# Recording

> Capture a session and export per-player tracks as BWAV or MP4/Opus.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/creator/recording

The recording feature of Bedrock Voice Chat records a session with each player on a separate track. You can mix and edit each voice separately.

:::note
Recording is available only on Windows, macOS and Linux. Mobile devices cannot write multi-track audio to storage fast enough.
:::

## Start a recording

Press **REC** at the bottom of the secondary sidebar. The indicator turns red.

A session records player positions and group data with the audio. The export can put each voice at the position where the player stood.

You can also start and stop a recording [in game](/wiki/player/in-game-commands/) with `/bvc:record <on|off>`, or from a [Stream Deck](/wiki/creator/stream-deck/).

## Server policy

An operator can stop all players on their server from recording:

```hcl
voice {
    recording {
        enabled = false
    }
}
```

Recording is allowed by default. On a server older than 1.0.0-beta.21, recording is allowed.

:::caution
The client applies this setting. The server cannot enforce it. Recordings are saved on the player's own computer and never go to the server.

When `enabled = false`, the standard client disables the REC button, `/bvc:record`, and the WebSocket `record` action. A modified client or a screen recorder can still record.
:::

See [configuration](/wiki/reference/configuration/#voicerecording).

## Manage recordings

Open **Settings → Recordings**.

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/settings-recordings.jpg" alt="Recordings page listing sessions with their participants" /></div>

**Recordings** lists your sessions and their participants. You can rename, delete and export each session.

The list shows each session by its timestamp until you give it a name. If you clear the name, the list shows the timestamp again.

The export writes each track to a separate file. To export only some tracks, expand the track list and select them.

| Track | Contents |
|---|---|
| Your own | Your microphone. |
| Player | The voice of one other player. |
| Jukebox | Music from a jukebox. |

Each player track has the player's name. A player who is signed in on two devices records as two tracks.

When an export is complete, BVC opens the output folder:

| System | Folder |
|---|---|
| Windows | `%localappdata%/com.alaydriem.bvc.client/recordings/<session_uuid>/renders` |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/com.alaydriem.bvc.client/recordings/<session_uuid>/renders` |
| Linux | `~/.local/share/com.alaydriem.bvc.client/recordings/<session_uuid>/renders` |

## Spatial export

**Mix in the spatial positions** puts each voice at the position where the player stood, and writes each track in stereo. It is on by default.

Turn it off to write each track in mono at the centre, directly from the recording, with no re-encoding. Use this if you want to position the voices yourself.

A spatial export needs two values that are not in the recording: the server's spatial audio settings and your panning intensity. BVC uses the values from the live session. If there is no live session, it uses the last known values, and then the defaults. The export log shows which values it used.

If the export uses the defaults, and the server uses a different `broadcast_range`, the volume of each voice over distance is wrong in the export. You cannot hear this error easily. If an export sounds wrong, read the export log.

See [`voice.spatial_audio`](/wiki/reference/configuration/#voicespatial_audio).

## Format version

Each session stores the format version that it was recorded with. To export a session, this version must be the same as the version of your app.

:::caution
**A BVC update can stop you from exporting older sessions.** The sessions stay on disk and stay in the list, but the export is refused. To export them, install the earlier version of the app.

Export the sessions that you want to keep before you update.
:::

## Export formats

| Format | Notes |
|---|---|
| **BWAV** (`.wav`) | Broadcast WAV with timecode. Uncompressed PCM. Large and lossless. All editors accept it. |
| **MP4 / Opus** | Opus in an MP4 container, with timecode. Much smaller. |

Both formats have timecode. The tracks align on an editor timeline with no manual synchronisation.

## Disk space

BWAV is uncompressed PCM. It uses approximately 5–15 MB for each player for each 30 seconds. A two-hour session with six players makes 7–21 GB.

To use less disk space:

- Export to MP4/Opus, unless your editor needs PCM.
- Split long sessions into shorter recordings.
- Delete old exports. BVC does not delete them automatically.

## Consent

:::danger
Any member of a group can record all members of that group, and BVC does not notify them. A player can also record nearby players, and BVC does not notify them.

Tell people when you record. The law where you and the other players live can require their consent. Bedrock Voice Chat does not ask for consent and does not notify players.
:::

---

# Stream Deck

> Control mute, deafen, recording, jukebox music, world connection, and live stats from an Elgato Stream Deck.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/creator/stream-deck

The Bedrock Voice Chat Stream Deck plugin lets you control the app from an Elgato Stream Deck. It has six actions: **Microphone**, **Deafen**, **Record**, **Jukebox**, **Connect**, and **Stats**.

Download it from the [Elgato Marketplace](https://marketplace.elgato.com/product/bedrock-voice-chat-c5a151d6-3669-487f-9548-bfe689e50203). Releases and issues are in the [plugin repository](https://github.com/Alaydriem/bedrock-voice-chat-streamdeck).

## Enable the WebSocket server

The WebSocket server is off by default. Open **Settings → WebSocket server** and turn it on.

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/settings-websocket.jpg" alt="WebSocket settings page with the server enabled, showing port and key" /></div>

Write down the port and the authentication key.

## Configure the plugin

Install the plugin, then enter the same port and authentication key. If BVC is on a different computer from the Stream Deck, also set the host.

## Actions

| Action | Controls | Setup |
|---|---|---|
| Microphone | Your microphone. | None |
| Deafen | All incoming audio. | None |
| Record | Session recording. | None |
| Jukebox | Jukebox music. | None |
| Connect | The world that BVC is connected to. | Select the world. |
| Stats | Nothing. Shows one live number. | Select the stat. |

Each key has an image for on, off, and disconnected. Disconnected means that the plugin cannot connect to BVC. Make sure that the app is running and the WebSocket server is on.

Set up Connect and Stats in each key's settings in the Stream Deck app.

## Microphone and push-to-talk

The Microphone key follows the voice mode. In open mic mode, it mutes and unmutes. In push-to-talk mode, it opens the microphone when you press it and closes the microphone when you release it.

Deafen and Jukebox work in both modes.

## Jukebox

The Jukebox key mutes or unmutes all jukebox music for you. Other players and voice audio are not affected.

To set the jukebox volume, use the app, or use the in-game command: `/bvc:jukeboxvolume` on Bedrock or `/bvc jukebox volume` on Java. See [using the jukebox](/wiki/player/using-the-jukebox/).

## Connect

Select a Realm or a server in the key's settings. Press the key to connect to it. Press the key again to disconnect.

The list comes from BVC. Start the app before you open the key's settings.

## Stats

Each Stats key shows one number. To show a second number, add a second Stats key.

Select the stat from the list in the key's settings. The list contains the values that BVC sends now. If the list is empty, press refresh.

A number changes to `—` when it is more than three seconds old, or when the plugin loses its connection.

Stats come from the `/metrics` route of the WebSocket server. When you turn on the WebSocket server, commands and stats both work.

## Other actions

BVC also accepts a jukebox volume level, and group create, join and leave. The plugin has no keys for these actions. The [WebSocket API](/wiki/creator/websocket-api/) page lists all actions.

## Recording availability

Recording is available only on desktop. The Record key does nothing when BVC runs on a mobile device, or when the server has [turned recording off](/wiki/creator/recording/).

## Two computers

If BVC runs on your gaming PC and the Stream Deck is on a streaming PC, set the host to the LAN address of the gaming PC. Allow the port through the firewall on the gaming PC.

Only the authentication key protects the WebSocket server. Do not make the port reachable from outside your LAN.

## Your own tools

Any program that can use WebSocket can use the same API. See [WebSocket API](/wiki/creator/websocket-api/).

---

# WebSocket API

> Drive mute, deafen, recording, jukebox music, and groups from your own tooling.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/creator/websocket-api

Bedrock Voice Chat runs a local WebSocket server. Your own tools can use it to toggle mute, deafen and recording, set the jukebox music level, manage groups, hold push-to-talk, and start or stop a Bedrock Voice Chat Connect session. The [Stream Deck plugin](/wiki/creator/stream-deck/) uses this server.

## Reference

The full reference is at [bedrockvoicechat.com/websocket](https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/websocket).

## Enable the server

The WebSocket server is off by default. Open **Settings → WebSocket server** and turn it on.

Write down the port and the authentication key. Every message must contain the key. The server rejects a message without a valid key.

<div class="window"><img src="/assets/wiki/settings-websocket.jpg" alt="WebSocket settings page with the server enabled, showing port and key" /></div>

## Routes

The server has two endpoints on the same port.

| Path | Direction | Authentication |
|---|---|---|
| Any path except `/metrics` | Request and response | Per message, as `key` |
| `/metrics` | Push only | At the upgrade, as `?key=` |

Only the exact path `/metrics` goes to the diagnostics stream. All other paths, including `/` and `/ws`, go to the command protocol. An integration that connects on any other path continues to work.

## Message format

Each message is one JSON object with an `action` field:

```json
{ "action": "mute", "device": "input", "key": "<your key>" }
```

There are thirteen actions: `ping`, `mute`, `record`, `jukebox`, `jukeboxvolume`, `state`, `ptt`, `targets`, `connect`, `disconnect`, `creategroup`, `joingroup`, `leavegroup`.

**Deafen is not a separate action.** To deafen, send `mute` with `device: "output"`. `input` is your microphone. `output` is all incoming audio.

## State

`mute`, `record`, `jukebox`, `jukeboxvolume`, `ptt`, `connect`, `disconnect`, and the three group actions send the new state to every connected client. A Stream Deck and your own tool stay in sync without polling.

Send `state` after you connect to get the current state. It reports `muted`, `deafened`, `recording`, `voice_mode`, `ptt_active`, `jukebox_muted`, `jukebox_gain`, and `connection`.

## Voice mode

`state` contains `voice_mode`, either `openMic` or `pushToTalk`. **Read it before you draw a microphone button.**

| Mode | Input mute | `ptt` |
|---|---|---|
| `openMic` | Works | Refused |
| `pushToTalk` | Refused | Controls the microphone |

Both refusals return an error that gives the reason. If you send an input mute in `pushToTalk`, the error tells you to send `ptt`.

Output mute always works.

### Push-to-talk

`ptt` takes `down`: `true` when the button is pressed, `false` when it is released.

Always send the release. A lost connection does not close the microphone. A button that stays down keeps the microphone open.

## Jukebox music

One setting controls all jukeboxes that the client plays. Voices are not affected.

| Action | Takes | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `jukebox` | nothing | Toggles mute. |
| `jukeboxvolume` | `level`, 0–150 | Sets the level. |

`jukebox` toggles mute. To get the current state before you draw a button, send `state` and read `jukebox_muted`.

Both actions reply with `muted` and `gain`. **Send `level` as a percentage. `gain` comes back as a fraction.** If you send 150, you get 1.5.

Mute and level are separate. A level that you set while muted applies when you unmute.

## Groups

| Action | Takes | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `creategroup` | `name` | Creates a group and joins it. |
| `joingroup` | `name` | Joins an existing group. |
| `leavegroup` | nothing | Leaves the current group. |

All three reply with `in_group`. If the client is in a group, the reply also has `id` and `name`.

`creategroup` and `joingroup` first remove the client from its current group.

`joingroup` is refused if the name matches no group, or more than one group. The match ignores case.

For a [Private Group](/wiki/player/groups/#private-groups), `joingroup` opens the join dialog in the app and sends the request. The client joins only after a member admits it.

## Connect to a world

`targets` lists the worlds that this client can join: saved servers, servers that the BVC server advertises, and your Realms. Each entry has an opaque `id`, a `name`, and a `kind` of `proxy` or `realm`.

`connect` takes an `id` from that list. **Send the `id`, not the list position.** The list can change between `targets` and `connect`.

`disconnect` stops the live session. It takes no target. Idempotent; safe to send when nothing is connected.

Both reply with `connected`. If there was a session, the reply also has `id` and `name`. Every `state` message has the same values in `state.connection`.

## Metrics stream

The metrics stream sends diagnostics only. You do not send requests. Connect and read.

```
ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/metrics?key=<your key>
```

Put the key in the query string. You send no messages on this stream. If the key is missing or wrong, the connection is refused.

If no key is set in BVC, `/metrics` accepts connections without a key.

Each message contains microphone, playback, connection quality, session and transport diagnostics, with round-trip time and packet-loss values. The message format is in the [reference](https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/websocket).

The command protocol does not change. Each command message still needs the key.

## Security

:::danger
Only the key protects the WebSocket server. Anyone who can reach the port and has the key can mute you, start a recording, or read your diagnostics stream.

Keep the port on your LAN. Do **not** forward it on your router.
:::

## Recording availability

`record` does nothing on a client that cannot record. Recording is available only on desktop.

`record` also does nothing when the connected server sets `voice.recording.enabled = false`. The client does not start a recording, and returns the current state. See [recording](/wiki/creator/recording/).

---

# CLI

> Command-line reference for the server executable: identities, users, permissions, and bootstrapping.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/reference/cli

The Bedrock Voice Chat server executable is also a command-line tool. Use it to manage identities, users and permissions on the local server or on a remote server.

Available since beta.11.

## Global flags

| Flag | Env | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-c, --config-file <path>` | None | `config.hcl` | Used only by `server` and `admin *`. |
| `--server-url <url>` | `BVC_SERVER` | `https://127.0.0.1:3000` | The server that `login` connects to. Set it to your server's URL. Other commands read the URL from the stored identity. |
| `--identity <gamertag:game>` | `BVC_IDENTITY` | None | The stored identity to use when there is more than one. |

## Identity

| Command | Auth | Transport | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `login` | None | `POST /api/auth/code` | Exchanges a one-time code for an mTLS certificate bundle and stores it. |
| `logout` | mTLS | Local | Deletes the active stored identity. |
| `whoami` | mTLS | `GET /api/auth/introspect` | Prints the identity, server URL, certificate expiry, and effective permissions. |

`login` takes one flag, `--code <code>`. If you do not give the flag, `login` asks for the code on stdin.

`login` needs only the code. The server finds the player from the code and returns the gamertag and the game.

## Server

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `server` | Starts the BVC server (HTTP and QUIC). Reads `--config-file`. |

## Bootstrap

These commands connect directly to the database. Run them on the server host, with `config.hcl` available. Use them when no admin exists yet.

| Command | Flags | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `admin bootstrap` | `-p, --player <name>`; `-g, --game <minecraft>` | Gives `admin` to the player. Creates the player record if it does not exist. |
| `admin generate-code` | `-p, --player <name>`; `-g, --game <minecraft>`; `-d, --duration <secs>`; `--ephemeral <true\|false>` | Makes a one-time login code. Creates the player record if it does not exist. |

`-d` has a default of 3600.

`--ephemeral` has a default of `true`: the code is used up when it is redeemed. Pass `--ephemeral false` to make a code that stays valid until it expires and can be used more than one time.

## Users

These commands use HTTPS with mTLS. They need an active admin identity (`whoami` shows `admin`).

| Command | Endpoint | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `user add` | `POST /api/admin/user` | Creates a player with a certificate and a keypair. Returns 409 if the player exists. |
| `user banish` | `PATCH /api/admin/user/banish` | Sets or clears the banished flag. |
| `user generate-code` | `POST /api/admin/user/code` | Makes a login code for an existing player. Returns 404 if the player does not exist. |

Flags: `-p, --player <name>` and `-g, --game <minecraft>`. `user banish` also takes `-b, --banish <true|false>` (default `true`). `user generate-code` also takes `-d, --duration <secs>` (default 3600) and `--ephemeral <true|false>` (default `true`).

## Permissions

These commands need an active admin identity. Valid permission names: `audio_upload`, `audio_delete`, `admin`.

| Command | Endpoint | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `permission allow` | `PUT /api/admin/permission` | Sets an allow override. |
| `permission deny` | `PUT /api/admin/permission` | Sets a deny override. |
| `permission clear` | `DELETE /api/admin/permission` | Removes the override. The config default then applies. |
| `permission list` | `GET /api/admin/permission/{game}` | Lists the overrides. |

Flags: `-p, --player <name>` and `-g, --game <minecraft>`. All commands except `list` also take `--permission <name>`.

If `list` prints nothing, the player has no overrides. Only the config defaults apply.

## Peering

These commands use HTTPS with mTLS. They need an active admin identity.

| Command | Endpoint | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `relay peerlink` | `GET /api/admin/relay/peerlink` | Prints this server's peer link, its node ID, and a `peers` block to paste into the other server's `config.hcl`. |
| `relay worlds` | `GET /api/admin/relay/worlds` | Lists relay worlds with player counts. |

`relay peerlink` takes `-l, --label <label>`. This is the block label in the printed example. The default is `bvc-server`. Set the label to the name that the other server uses for this server.

`relay peerlink` exits with a non-zero code on a server that has no `peers` block in `config.hcl`. The peer endpoint binds only when a `peers` block exists.

`relay worlds` prints nothing until a player joins a relay world.

See [peering](/wiki/reference/peering/).

## Bootstrapping a new deployment

```bash
# Server host, config.hcl available
bvc admin generate-code -p Alice -g minecraft -d 3600
# -> Code: ABCD1234

# Anywhere with network access
bvc login --code ABCD1234

# Server host
bvc admin bootstrap -p Alice -g minecraft

# Alice now has admin
bvc whoami
bvc user add -p Bob -g minecraft
bvc user generate-code -p Bob -g minecraft
```

See [players and permissions](/wiki/server/players-and-permissions/).

---

# Configuration reference

> Every block and key in config.hcl, with defaults.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/reference/configuration

The Bedrock Voice Chat server reads these blocks and keys from `config.hcl`. Almost no key is required. For a working example, see [Installing the BVC server](/wiki/server/installation/).

Most keys also have an environment variable. See [environment variables](/wiki/reference/environment-variables/). Precedence: **environment, then config file, then default**.

The server reads `config.hcl` one time, at startup. Restart the server after you edit it.

## Environment interpolation

You can use `${env.VAR}` anywhere in the file:

```hcl
minecraft {
    access_token = "${env.BVC_ACCESS_TOKEN}"
}
```

If a referenced variable is not set, the server does not start.

## `server`

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `listen` | `::` | Bind address. The IPv6 wildcard also accepts IPv4 connections. |
| `port` | `443` | Public TCP port for the HTTP API and login. The server accepts TLS on this port and forwards API requests to an internal listener on a loopback port. |
| `quic_port` | `28280` | UDP port for QUIC voice. |
| `advertised_quic_ports` | `[28280]` | Public UDP ports that clients try, in order of preference. Clients get only the ports in this list. `quic_port` is not added. The default stays `[28280]` when you change `quic_port`. Set this list when you change `quic_port`, or when a proxy receives traffic on a different port. An empty list publishes only `quic_port`. |
| `assets_path` | `./assets` | Directory of static files that the API serves. |

With the default `::`, QUIC uses one socket for IPv4 and IPv6. On Linux, this depends on `net.ipv6.bindv6only`, which is `0` by default.

## `server.tls`

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `certificate` | None | Path to a full-chain PEM file. Required unless `acme` is set. |
| `key` | None | Path to the private key PEM file. Required unless `acme` is set. |
| `names` | `["localhost"]` | Hostnames that clients use to reach the server. The server puts them in the certificate. |
| `ips` | `["127.0.0.1"]` | IP addresses that clients use to reach the server. The server puts them in the certificate. |
| `certs_path` | `./certificates` | Directory for the mTLS CA (`ca.crt`) that authenticates clients. The server manages this directory. |
| `acme` | None | Automatic certificates. Do not use with `certificate` and `key`. |

## `server.tls.acme`

Gets and renews a certificate with ACME DNS-01. You do not need to open port 80. If you set `acme` and also `certificate` or `key`, the server does not start.

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `email` | None | ACME account contact email. **Required.** |
| `provider` | None | `cloudflare` or `acme-dns`. **Required.** |
| `api_token` | None | Cloudflare only. An API token for one zone, with DNS edit permission. |
| `server_url` | None | acme-dns only. |
| `username` | None | acme-dns only. |
| `password` | None | acme-dns only. |
| `subdomain` | None | acme-dns only. |
| `directory` | `https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory` | ACME directory URL. Use the staging directory during tests to avoid rate limits. |
| `domains` | DNS entries of `tls.names` | Certificate domains. The server skips IP entries in `tls.names`. An ACME certificate cannot contain an IP address. |

The server checks the provider fields at startup. If a field is missing, the error names it.

## `server.minecraft`

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `access_token` | None | Shared secret that the Addon sends as `Authorization: Bearer`. **Required.** |
| `client_id` | `a17f9693-f01f-4d1d-ad12-1f179478375d` | Microsoft OAuth2 client ID. **Do not change.** All released apps authenticate with this public BVC client ID. |

## `server.features`

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `chat` | `true` | Sends in-game chat between the game and the app. See [Chat](/wiki/player/chat/). |
| `openapi_docs` | `false` | Serves `/openapi.json` and the API browser at `/docs`. |
| `radar` | `true` | Shows players beyond voice range on the dashboard ring. See [radar](#radar). |
| `telemetry` | `true` | Anonymous usage metrics. See [privacy and telemetry](/wiki/server/privacy-and-telemetry/). |

With `chat = false`, the server sends no chat in either direction. The server drops chat messages from the Addon and refuses chat messages from the app. The Addon's chat connection still opens, but it is not used. You do not change the Addon or mod configuration.

The app reads the `chat` setting when it connects. The chat panel stays on the dashboard, greyed out, and shows `Chat is disabled on this server`.

### `radar`

The dashboard ring shows players who are beyond voice range. The server still sends the positions of these players to the client. With `radar = false`, the ring is empty. The player list does not change.

`radar` changes only the display. A modified client can still show those players.

The server publishes this value on `/api/config` as `radar.enabled`. If a client cannot read the config, it shows the ring, the same as with an older server.

### Code login

One-time code login (`POST /api/auth/code`, used by `bvc login`) is always on. Earlier releases had a `code_login` flag for it. That key no longer exists. The server ignores it.

## `server.peers`

Declared peers, one labelled block for each peer. The server does not find peers automatically. It refuses a connection from any server that is not in this list.

:::caution[Work in progress]
The format of this block changes between releases. See [peering](/wiki/reference/peering/).
:::

```hcl
server {
    peers "partner-smp" {
        peerlink     = "<base32 peer link>"
        worlds       = ["overworld"]
        capabilities = ["carry_speakers"]
    }
}
```

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `peerlink` | None | The peer link that the other server printed. It contains that server's public key and its network addresses. **Required.** |
| `worlds` | `[]` | Limits the link to some of the peer's worlds. An empty list accepts all worlds that the peer declares. |
| `capabilities` | `["carry_speakers"]` | The actions that the peer can do on the link. |

Get `peerlink` from the other server with `bvc relay peerlink`. The command prints a block that you can paste. See the [CLI reference](/wiki/reference/cli/).

Log lines use the block label as the name of the peer.

### `worlds`

During the handshake, a peer declares the worlds that it hosts. `worlds` limits which of those worlds this server accepts.

| Value | Effect |
|---|---|
| `[]` | Accept every world that the peer declares. |
| `["a", "b"]` | Accept only the worlds that are in this list and in the peer's declaration. |

`worlds` cannot add a world that the peer did not declare.

### `capabilities`

| Value | Effect |
|---|---|
| `carry_speakers` | Sends voice across the link. |
| `query_audio` | Reserved. Has no effect. |
| `serve_audio` | Reserved. Has no effect. |

If you omit the key, the peer gets `carry_speakers`. An empty list gives the peer nothing.

If a value is not recognised, the server does not start, and the error names the value.

Peers do not fetch audio files. The server that plays Jukebox audio decodes it and sends it to peers as normal voice audio.

## `server.enrollment`

`server.enrollment` gets a hostname and a certificate for a server that has no domain. See [assigned hostnames](/wiki/server/enrollment/).

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `token` | None | The single-use enrollment token. The server uses it at first start. |
| `address` | None | The address to publish as the A record of the assigned name. |

Use only one certificate source: `enrollment.token`, `tls.acme`, or `tls.certificate` with `tls.key`. If you set more than one, the server does not start.

`address` is optional. If you do not set it, BVC publishes no DNS record. BVC clients can reach the server without the record. Only a Bedrock Addon with `addon_mode = "net"` on a different host needs the name to resolve. BVC publishes a private address but does not check it. BVC checks a public address every day.

### Registry address

The BVC registry address is compiled into the binary. No config key or environment variable changes it. To use a different registry, rebuild the server.

## `server.peering` and `server.peer_port`

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `peering` | `true` | Binds the peer endpoint when no peer is declared. Another server can then pair with this server. |
| `peer_port` | `28284` | UDP port of the peer endpoint. `0` asks the system for a random port. |

With `peering = false`, the peer endpoint binds only when `server.peers` declares at least one peer.

The peer link contains this port. A random port changes at each restart, and the peer link that the other server has becomes invalid. For this reason, the default is a fixed port. Open or forward this port when peers connect to this server directly.

## `server.cors`

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `allowed_origins` | `[]` | Allowed origins. An empty list allows all origins. The BVC client uses mTLS and is not affected. |
| `allow_credentials` | `true` | Sends `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials`. |

## `server.age`

The minimum age for your community. Clients use it to decide when to show Age Signals (Android) or Declared Age Ranges (iOS) prompts.

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `minimum` | `13` | Minimum age. `0` turns off the age check. The server changes any other value to the nearest value from 13 to 18. |

## `server.bedrock`

The server list that clients see in Bedrock Voice Chat Connect, and the maximum age of position events from Connect.

Bedrock support is always on. No key turns it off.

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `proxy_event_freshness_threshold_secs` | `30` | The server discards a position event from Connect that is older than this number of seconds. |
| `servers` | `[]` | The server list that the server sends to clients. |

### `server.bedrock.servers`

```hcl
bedrock {
    servers = [
        {
            name             = "My SMP"
            host             = "play.example.com"
            port             = 19132
            protocol_version = 1001
            addon_mode       = "net"
        }
    ]
}
```

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | None | Name shown in the client. |
| `host` | None | Hostname of the Bedrock server. |
| `port` | `19132` | Port of the Bedrock server. |
| `protocol_version` | None | The protocol version that the BVC client shows to Minecraft. If you omit it, the client uses the version of the Bedrock server (Auto). See [version support](/wiki/platforms/version-support/). |
| `addon_mode` | None | `net` or `no_net`. **Required.** Selects how events for this world reach the BVC server. |

`addon_mode` selects how position, state and chat events for the world reach the BVC server.

| Value | Delivery |
|---|---|
| `net` | The world's BVC Addon sends events to the BVC server over HTTP. Connect only forwards game traffic. |
| `no_net` | The world has no HTTP connection. Connect reads the events from the game traffic and sends them. |

You must set `addon_mode`. The server cannot detect it. The server identifies a running Addon by the UUID of its world, and it cannot match that UUID to an entry in `servers`.

`addon_mode` does not change how a client connects to the BVC server.

`addon_mode` has no default. Each entry must set it. If one entry does not set it, the server cannot read the `servers` list.

Use `no_net` for Realms and Aternos worlds that run the no-net Addon. Use `net` for a world that runs the standard Addon or the Java mod.

## `database`

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `scheme` | `sqlite3` | `sqlite`, `sqlite3`, `mysql`, `postgres`, or `postgresql`. |
| `database` | `./bvc.sqlite3` | SQLite path, or database name. |
| `host` | `127.0.0.1` | MySQL and Postgres only. |
| `port` | `3306` / `5432` | Default for each scheme. |
| `username` | None | MySQL and Postgres only. |
| `password` | None | MySQL and Postgres only. |
| `ssl_mode` | None | `disable`, `prefer`, `require`, `verify-ca`, `verify-full`. |
| `ssl_root_cert` | None | CA certificate that verifies the database server. |
| `ssl_cert` | None | Client certificate for database mTLS. |
| `ssl_key` | None | Key for `ssl_cert`. |

The server checks the database TLS settings at startup. It rejects these combinations:

- Any `ssl_*` path without `ssl_mode`. Without `ssl_mode`, the connection can fall back to plaintext.
- `ssl_root_cert` with a mode weaker than `verify-ca`. The server would never check the CA.
- `ssl_cert` without `ssl_key`, or a path to a file that does not exist.
- Any `ssl_*` option with a SQLite scheme.

## `log`

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `level` | `info` | `trace`, `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`. `RUST_LOG` overrides it. |
| `path` | `./logs` | Directory for the rotating JSON log file. The server creates it if it does not exist. |

You cannot configure the console output. The server always writes human-readable output to stderr, and a JSON file to `log.path`. If the server cannot write to `log.path`, it writes logs only to the console and continues to run.

## `voice`

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `datagram_send_capacity` | `1024` | Size of the outgoing QUIC datagram queue for each connection. |
| `datagram_recv_capacity` | `1024` | Size of the incoming QUIC datagram queue for each connection. |
| `send_batch_wait_micros` | `7500` | Microseconds that the sender waits after the first queued datagram before it sends the batch. `0` sends each datagram immediately. |

A non-zero `send_batch_wait_micros` adds up to that many microseconds of latency. The server then sends fewer, larger UDP packets and uses less CPU. The client's playback buffer hides the default delay.

### `voice.recording`

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | Whether clients connected to this server can record. |

The client applies this setting. The server does not. Recordings are saved on the player's own computer and never go to the server. When `false`, the standard client does not start a recording from the REC button, `/bvc:record`, or the WebSocket API. A modified client can still record.

The server publishes this value on `/api/config`. If a client cannot read the config, it allows recording, the same as with an older server.

See [recording](/wiki/creator/recording/).

### `voice.limits`

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `connections` | `0` | Maximum number of voice sessions at the same time. `0` means no limit. |
| `reconnect_grace` | `60` | Number of seconds that a disconnected player keeps their slot. |

The limit counts players. One player on two devices uses one slot. The limit never refuses a player who reconnects, even while the old connection closes.

When the limit refuses a player, the client shows a notice about the limit and tries again. The player connects when a slot is free. The limit does not affect registration. New players are still added to the player list, and can sign in when there is a free slot.

`reconnect_grace` keeps the slot of a player who disconnected cleanly. Examples: the player closed the app, or Android stopped it in the background. A new player who arrives during that time does not take the slot. When no other slot is free, a new player gets a held slot. The oldest held slot is released first.

The server publishes these values on `/api/config` as `capacity.limit` and `capacity.in_use`. If a client cannot read the config, it treats the server as unlimited, the same as with an older server.

Players from a peer server do not use slots on this server. Their own server counts them. The limit does not apply to the HTTP API. You can administer a full server.

### `voice.spatial_audio`

All distances are in blocks.

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `broadcast_range` | `48.0` | Maximum distance at which the server sends audio. |
| `close_threshold` | `24.0` | Full volume at this distance or closer. |
| `falloff_distance` | `48.0` | Distance at which the volume reaches its minimum. |
| `steepen_start` | `38.0` | Distance where the volume drops faster towards silence. |
| `deafen_distance` | `3.0` | At distances below this, there is no stereo panning. |
| `panning_start` | `8.0` | Distance at which stereo panning starts to increase. |
| `max_attenuation_db` | `40.0` | Volume reduction at `falloff_distance`, in dB. |

Panning increases from `panning_start` to `close_threshold`. A higher `close_threshold` spreads voices across the stereo field over a wider range of distances.

## `audio`

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `file_path` | `./assets/audio` | Directory for uploaded audio clips. |
| `max_concurrent_per_uuid` | `5` | Maximum number of clips that one player can play at the same time. |

## `permissions`

```hcl
permissions {
    defaults = {
        audio_upload = true
        audio_delete = false
        admin        = false
    }
}
```

The server-wide defaults for the three permissions. Set overrides for one player with the `permission` CLI commands. See the [CLI reference](/wiki/reference/cli/).

| Permission | Grants |
|---|---|
| `audio_upload` | Upload clips to the audio library. |
| `audio_delete` | Delete clips from the library. |
| `admin` | Manage players and permissions. |

Peering is not a player permission. You declare a peer in [`server.peers`](/wiki/reference/configuration/#serverpeers).

---

# Environment variables

> Every BVC_* override, and how precedence works.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/reference/environment-variables

Most Bedrock Voice Chat configuration values have a `BVC_*` environment variable. With these variables, you can run a server without a config file. Precedence: **environment, then config file, then default**.

A variable that is not set, or that is empty, does not change a value. `FOO=` in a compose file does not clear a configured value. If a variable has an invalid value, the server does not start.

`config.hcl` is optional. With no file, the server uses the defaults and the environment variables, and writes a log line that says so. Kubernetes deployments usually work this way. See [Docker](/wiki/server/docker/).

## Server

| Variable | Sets |
|---|---|
| `BVC_SERVER` | `server.listen` and `server.port`, from a `host:port` value. The server ignores a URL value (`https://…`). The CLI reads a URL value as `--server-url`. |
| `BVC_QUIC_PORT` | `server.quic_port` |
| `BVC_ADVERTISED_QUIC_PORTS` | `server.advertised_quic_ports`. Comma-separated. |
| `BVC_ACCESS_TOKEN` | `server.minecraft.access_token` |
| `BVC_TELEMETRY` | `server.features.telemetry`. `true` or `false`. |
| `BVC_CHAT` | `server.features.chat`. `true` or `false`. |
| `BVC_RADAR` | `server.features.radar`. `true` or `false`. |

## Voice

| Variable | Sets |
|---|---|
| `BVC_RECORDING` | `voice.recording.enabled`. `true` or `false`. |
| `BVC_MAX_CONNECTIONS` | `voice.limits.connections`. The maximum number of voice sessions at the same time. `0` means no limit. |
| `BVC_RECONNECT_GRACE` | `voice.limits.reconnect_grace`. The number of seconds that a disconnected player keeps their slot. |

## Runtime

Only the Java mod's embedded server reads these variables. A standalone server ignores them.

| Variable | Sets |
|---|---|
| `BVC_RUNTIME_WORKER_THREADS` | Number of Tokio worker threads. The default is the number of CPU cores on the host. |
| `BVC_RUNTIME_MAX_BLOCKING_THREADS` | Maximum number of threads in the blocking pool. |

## TLS

| Variable | Sets |
|---|---|
| `BVC_TLS_CERTIFICATE` | `server.tls.certificate` |
| `BVC_TLS_KEY` | `server.tls.key` |
| `BVC_TLS_CERTS_PATH` | `server.tls.certs_path` |
| `BVC_TLS_NAMES` | `server.tls.names`. Comma-separated. |
| `BVC_TLS_IPS` | `server.tls.ips`. Comma-separated. |

## Enrollment

In a container, set the enrollment token with these variables. See [assigned hostnames](/wiki/server/enrollment/).

| Variable | Sets |
|---|---|
| `BVC_ENROLLMENT_TOKEN` | `server.enrollment.token` |
| `BVC_ENROLLMENT_ADDRESS` | `server.enrollment.address` |

Use only one certificate source: an enrollment token, ACME, or a TLS certificate and key. If you set more than one, the server does not start.

`BVC_REGISTRY_PEERLINK` has no effect on a running server. It is read only when the binary is compiled.

## ACME

If the config file has no `acme` block, setting any of these variables creates one. A new `acme` block needs both `BVC_ACME_EMAIL` and `BVC_ACME_PROVIDER`. If one is missing, the server does not start, and the error names the missing variable.

| Variable | Sets |
|---|---|
| `BVC_ACME_EMAIL` | Account contact email. |
| `BVC_ACME_PROVIDER` | `cloudflare` or `acme-dns`. |
| `BVC_ACME_API_TOKEN` | Cloudflare API token. |
| `BVC_ACME_DIRECTORY` | ACME directory URL. |
| `BVC_ACME_DOMAINS` | Certificate domains. Comma-separated. |
| `BVC_ACME_DNS_URL` | acme-dns server URL. |
| `BVC_ACME_DNS_USERNAME` | acme-dns username. |
| `BVC_ACME_DNS_PASSWORD` | acme-dns password. |
| `BVC_ACME_DNS_SUBDOMAIN` | acme-dns subdomain. |

See [TLS](/wiki/server/tls/).

## Database

| Variable | Sets |
|---|---|
| `BVC_DATABASE_SCHEME` | `database.scheme` |
| `BVC_DATABASE_DATABASE` | `database.database` |
| `BVC_DATABASE_HOST` | `database.host` |
| `BVC_DATABASE_PORT` | `database.port` |
| `BVC_DATABASE_USERNAME` | `database.username` |
| `BVC_DATABASE_PASSWORD` | `database.password` |
| `BVC_DATABASE_SSL_MODE` | `database.ssl_mode` |
| `BVC_DATABASE_SSL_ROOT_CERT` | `database.ssl_root_cert` |
| `BVC_DATABASE_SSL_CERT` | `database.ssl_cert` |
| `BVC_DATABASE_SSL_KEY` | `database.ssl_key` |

The server checks the TLS settings at startup. See the [database section](/wiki/reference/configuration/#database) for the combinations that it rejects.

## Bedrock

| Variable | Sets |
|---|---|
| `BVC_BEDROCK_SERVERS` | Replaces the whole server list. |

`BVC_BEDROCK_SERVERS` takes comma-separated `Name@host[:port][@protocol][@mode]` entries:

```
BVC_BEDROCK_SERVERS="My SMP@play.example.com:19132@1001@net,Other@mc.example.net@no_net"
```

`protocol` is a protocol version number. `mode` is `net` or `no_net`. If you omit `mode`, it is `net`. You can omit `protocol`, `mode`, or both, and you can write them in either order. If a value is not a number, `net` or `no_net`, the server does not start, and the error names the value. See [`server.bedrock.servers`](/wiki/reference/configuration/#serverbedrockservers).

Use a hostname. Do not use an IPv6 address. The parser reads its colons as a port separator.

## Meridian

`BVC_MERIDIAN_*` configures registration with Meridian, the proxy for BVC managed hosting. A self-hosted server does not use these variables.

## CLI variables

The CLI reads these variables. The server does not.

| Variable | Used by |
|---|---|
| `BVC_SERVER` | `--server-url` for `login`. The server also reads `BVC_SERVER` (see [Server](#server)). A URL value is for the CLI. A `host:port` value is for the server. |
| `BVC_IDENTITY` | `--identity`, as `<gamertag>:<game>`. |
| `BVC_IDENTITY_DIR` | The directory for stored CLI identities. |

See [CLI](/wiki/reference/cli/).

## Environment interpolation

You can use `${env.VAR}` anywhere in `config.hcl`:

```hcl
minecraft {
    access_token = "${env.BVC_ACCESS_TOKEN}"
}
```

If a referenced variable is not set, the server does not start.

---

# HTTP API

> Location of the BVC server API reference, and its authentication schemes.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/reference/http-api

The Bedrock Voice Chat server has an HTTP API for authentication, configuration, player positions, and administration.

## Reference

The full API reference is at [bedrockvoicechat.com/api](https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/api).

## Serving the spec from your own server

Your server can serve the spec for its own build:

```hcl
server {
    features {
        openapi_docs = true
    }
}
```

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `/openapi.json` | The OpenAPI spec. |
| `/docs` | A browsable UI for the spec. |

## Authentication

| Scheme | Used by |
|---|---|
| **mTLS** | Player and admin endpoints. The server issues the client certificate at login. |
| **`Authorization: Bearer`** | Endpoints that the Addon or the Java mod calls to send player positions. The token is the value of `server.minecraft.access_token`. |
| **None** | Health, config, and the login endpoints. |

---

# Peering

> Linking two BVC servers so voice carries across both. Work in progress.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/reference/peering

:::caution[Work in progress]
Peering is in development. The configuration, the CLI, and the protocol change between releases. Do not use peering on a production community.
:::

Peering links two Bedrock Voice Chat servers. Players whose worlds overlap can then hear each other across both servers.

## Peer declaration

Servers do not find each other automatically. Each operator adds the other server's peer link to their own `config.hcl`. A server refuses a connection from any server that is not in that list.

A server that is listed in `server.peers` can connect. No player permission controls peering.

## Link two servers

On server A, run:

```bash
bvc relay peerlink --label server-a
```

The command prints the peer link, the server's node ID, and a `peers` block. Paste the block into server B's `config.hcl`. Then run the same command on server B with `--label server-b`, and paste its block into server A's `config.hcl`.

Restart both servers.

Server A's `config.hcl`:

```hcl
server {
    peers "server-b" {
        peerlink = "<the value server B printed>"
    }
}
```

## Configuration

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `peerlink` | None | The peer link that the other server printed. **Required.** |
| `worlds` | `[]` | Limits the link to some of the worlds that the peer declares. |
| `capabilities` | `["carry_speakers"]` | The actions that the peer can do on the link. |

See the [configuration reference](/wiki/reference/configuration/#serverpeers) for full descriptions.

## Network access

A peer link contains the addresses of its server. Two servers on one host, or two hosts on one local network, need nothing more.

Over the internet, the two servers connect directly. No relay forwards the traffic. No voice or position data goes through Bedrock Voice Chat infrastructure.

At least one server must accept incoming connections. If both servers are behind NAT, forward [`server.peer_port`](/wiki/reference/configuration/#serverpeering-and-serverpeer_port) (UDP `28284` by default) on one of them. If neither server can accept connections, peering does not work. This usually happens when both servers are behind carrier-grade NAT.

## Diagnostics

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `bvc relay peerlink` | Prints this server's peer link and node ID. |
| `bvc relay worlds` | Lists the relay worlds that this server hosts, with player counts. |

`bvc relay worlds` lists nothing until a player joins a relay world.

Both commands use the admin API over mTLS and need an active admin identity. See the [CLI reference](/wiki/reference/cli/).

## Moderation

Players on the peer server hear your players, and your players hear them. The moderation of each operator affects both communities. Declare a peer only when you trust the other operator's moderation.

---

# Upgrading

> Moving an existing Bedrock Voice Chat deployment to a newer release.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/upgrading

Bedrock Voice Chat releases the server, the client and the Minecraft mods together, with one version number. Upgrade all three to the same version.

## Version pairing

Use the same release everywhere. The voice protocol has its own version number, which is not the release version. The client compares the major and minor numbers of its voice protocol with those of the server. If they are different, the client refuses the session. A change to only the patch number does not affect compatibility.

| Release | Voice protocol |
|---|---|
| 1.0.0-beta.21 | 3.0.0 |
| 1.0.0-beta.20 | 2.1.0 |

On the server list, a client that is older than the server shows **Update needed**. A client that is newer than the server shows **Server is older**. In both cases, the client cannot connect.

## Procedure

1. Back up the database.
2. Stop the server.
3. Make the configuration changes listed in the release guide.
4. Replace the binary, or pull the new container image.
5. Start the server. Database migrations run at startup.
6. Read the startup log before you let players connect.
7. Update the Addon and any Java mod to the same release.

:::caution
Make the configuration changes **before** the first start on the new version. The server ignores most unknown keys and writes nothing to the log about them. Some removed keys stop the server. The release guide lists them.
:::

## Release guides

- [Upgrading to 1.0.0-beta.21](/wiki/upgrading/beta-21/)

---

# Upgrading to 1.0.0-beta.21

> Voice protocol 3.0.0, the peering rewrite, and every configuration key that changed since 1.0.0-beta.20.

Source: https://www.bedrockvoicechat.com/wiki/upgrading/beta-21

Bedrock Voice Chat 1.0.0-beta.21 changes the voice protocol, replaces the peering system, removes the Bedrock transfer relay, and moves several configuration keys.

## Upgrade steps

1. Back up the database.
2. Stop the server.
3. Add `addon_mode` to every entry in `server.bedrock.servers`. Use `"net"` or `"no_net"`. See [Bedrock Addon](#bedrock-addon) for the value to use. The server does not start without it.
4. Delete the `server.bedrock.dns` and `relay` blocks from `config.hcl`. Delete the `enabled`, `transfer_port`, `transfer_target_port` and `transfer_cache_ttl_secs` keys from `server.bedrock`. The server ignores these keys and shows no error for them.
5. Rename `log.out` to `log.path` in `config.hcl`. The server does not start while `out` is present.
6. Replace the server binary, or pull the new container image.
7. Start the server. Migrations run at startup.
8. Read the startup log before you let players connect.
9. Update the Bedrock Addon to 1.0.0-beta.21.
10. Tell your players to update the client to 1.0.0-beta.21. Older clients cannot connect.

:::danger
Do not skip step 1. Step 7 runs the `drop_peer_link_permission` migration, which deletes every `peer_link` grant. Its rollback restores nothing. No other record shows which players had the grant. Only your backup has it.
:::

Three deployment types need extra steps.

| Also running | Extra step |
|---|---|
| Java mod in embedded mode | Rewrite `embedded-config` as nested blocks before step 6. See [Java mod](#java-mod). |
| Peering | Link every pair of servers again with `bvc relay peerlink` after step 7. A 1.0.0-beta.20 peer link does not work in 1.0.0-beta.21. See [peering](#peering). |
| Hytale Java mod | Remove it. It is no longer built. |

No other key in `config.hcl` has to change.

## Voice protocol 3.0.0

The voice protocol changes from `2.1.0` to `3.0.0`. Clients on 1.0.0-beta.20 and earlier cannot open a session on a 1.0.0-beta.21 server. A 1.0.0-beta.21 client cannot open a session on an older server. Only the major and minor version numbers are compared.

No configuration key changes this. Update the server and the client together.

## Configuration changes

File: `config.hcl`

| Key | Change | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `server.bedrock.servers[].addon_mode` | New. **Required** on every entry. | Add `addon_mode = "net"` or `addon_mode = "no_net"` to each entry. |
| `server.bedrock.dns` | Removed. | Delete the block. |
| `server.bedrock.enabled` | Removed. Bedrock support is always on. | Delete the key. |
| `server.bedrock.transfer_port` | Removed with the transfer relay. | Delete the key. Close 28283/udp. |
| `server.bedrock.transfer_target_port` | Removed with the transfer relay. | Delete the key. |
| `server.bedrock.transfer_cache_ttl_secs` | Removed with the transfer relay. | Delete the key. |
| `relay` | Removed. Replaced by `server.peers` and `server.peer_relay_url`. | Delete the block. Declare the peers again. |
| `voice.recording` | New. `enabled` defaults to `true`. | Set `enabled = false` to stop clients from recording. |
| `voice.limits` | New. `connections` defaults to `0`. `0` sets no limit. | None. Set `connections` to limit the number of voice sessions. |
| `log.out` | Removed. Replaced by `log.path`. | Rename the key. See [Logging](#logging). |
| `log.path` | New. Directory for the log file. Defaults to `./logs`. | None, unless you want the file in a different directory. |

`addon_mode` has no default. If an entry in `servers` has no `addon_mode`, the server cannot read the configuration and does not start. All keys are in the [configuration reference](/wiki/reference/configuration/).

:::caution
The server ignores every other removed key. With a leftover `relay` block, `server.bedrock.dns` block, or `server.bedrock` transfer key, the server starts without those settings and writes nothing to the log.
:::

The `BVC_RECORDING` environment variable overrides `voice.recording.enabled`.

`voice.limits` needs no action. With no `voice.limits` block, the server has no connection limit, the same as 1.0.0-beta.20. The `BVC_MAX_CONNECTIONS` and `BVC_RECONNECT_GRACE` environment variables override `connections` and `reconnect_grace`. See [`voice.limits`](/wiki/reference/configuration/#voicelimits).

## Logging

The server now always writes to two outputs. You cannot turn off either output.

- **The console**, on **stderr**: human-readable text with colour.
- **A file**, in `log.path`: one JSON object per line.

### `log.path`

Old behaviour: `log.out = "stdout"` sent all output to standard output and nothing to a file. Any other value sent all output to a file and nothing to the console. Now the server always writes to both.

If `config.hcl` still contains `out`, the server **does not start**. The error names the key. `log.out` is the only removed key that stops the server.

```hcl
log {
    level = "info"
    path  = "./logs"
}
```

`log.path` is a directory. The server creates it if it does not exist. If the server cannot create or write to the directory, it writes one line to stderr and starts. It then logs only to the console.

### Console output

Standard output now contains only the output of CLI commands. The server log is on stderr. Update any supervisor unit, container configuration, or shell pipeline that read the server log from stdout. Docker, systemd and the Java mod capture both streams and need no change.

When stderr is not a terminal, the server does not write colour codes. `NO_COLOR=1` turns colour off. `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1` turns colour on.

### Log file format and rotation

Each line is one JSON object. `instance_id` and `name` come from `server.meridian`. They are `null` when that block is absent. `boot_id` changes each time the server process starts.

```json
{"ts":"2026-08-23T18:43:32.989Z","level":"info","target":"bvc_server_lib::runtime","msg":"Protocol Version: 3.0.0","instance_id":null,"name":null,"boot_id":"01a02fef-63fc-7ab3-80f0-76853ffb4bf2","file":"server/src/runtime/mod.rs","line":164}
```

Fields that belong to one log message are top-level keys. Read them with `jq`, for example `jq '.bind'`.

The log file rotates by size:

| Before | Now |
|---|---|
| `bvc-server.log.2026-08-23` | `bvc-server.log` plus `bvc-server_<timestamp>.log` archives |
| One file per day, kept forever | 50 MB per file, ten archives kept |

Update any logrotate rule or log collector pattern that matches the old names.

### `RUST_LOG`

`RUST_LOG` overrides `log.level` and the built-in log level of each library. It applies to log output from the server and from its libraries.

```
RUST_LOG=info,bvc_server_lib::stream=debug,hyper=off
```

A directive with no `=` sets the global level. A directive with `=` sets the level for each log target whose name starts with the text before `=`. The target is the `target` field in the JSON log. If more than one directive matches, the longest one applies. `off` turns a target off. If the server cannot read a directive, it names the directive on stderr and ignores it.

Only the `target=level` form is supported. The span and field syntax of some Rust tools (`target[span{field=value}]=level`) is not supported.

## Scripts that call the API

Three API changes affect your own scripts. Update any script that uses these routes. The 1.0.0-beta.21 Addon, Java mods and client already use the new form.

| Route | Change |
|---|---|
| `/api/position`, `/api/control`, `/api/state`, `/api/preferences`, `/api/audio/event`, the chat WebSocket | Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` instead of `X-MC-Access-Token: <token>`. The token value does not change. |
| `POST /api/bedrock/transfer` | Removed with the transfer relay. Delete the call. The client no longer needs it. |
| `GET /api/config` | `bedrock.transfer_port` is removed. `bedrock.enabled` stays and is always `true`. |

## QUIC ports

`server.advertised_quic_ports` sets the UDP ports that a client tries, in order of preference. If the list is not empty, clients try only the ports in the list. They do not try `server.quic_port` unless it is in the list. An empty list publishes only `quic_port`.

File: `config.hcl`

```hcl
server {
    quic_port = 443
    advertised_quic_ports = [443, 8443]
}
```

Use this list when a proxy receives traffic on a port that is not the bind port. The server binds one socket, however many ports it publishes.

The environment variable is `BVC_ADVERTISED_QUIC_PORTS`.

## WebSocket voice transport

Voice can now also use WebSocket on the HTTPS port. WebSocket uses `server.port` (443 by default) and needs no firewall change. The server always advertises it on `/api/config`. No key turns it off.

A client tries the published QUIC ports first. If it cannot connect on any QUIC port, it uses WebSocket.

### Forcing WebSocket-only voice

No setting turns off QUIC. To force WebSocket, make QUIC unreachable.

File: `config.hcl`

```hcl
server {
    quic_port = 0
    advertised_quic_ports = [1]
}
```

`quic_port = 0` binds the QUIC listener to a port that the operating system selects. `advertised_quic_ports = [1]` publishes a port where nothing listens. Every QUIC attempt fails, and voice uses WebSocket on 443.

:::note
Each client tries all published QUIC ports and waits for them to fail before it uses WebSocket. Sessions start more slowly.
:::

## Peering

:::caution
Peering is experimental and can change. Do not build anything on the peering protocol until a formal specification is announced.
:::

Peering is new in this release. A 1.0.0-beta.20 peer link does not work in 1.0.0-beta.21.

| 1.0.0-beta.20 | 1.0.0-beta.21 |
|---|---|
| `relay` config block | `server.peers` blocks and `server.peer_relay_url` |
| `POST /api/relay/offer` | Removed |
| `POST /api/relay/peer_link` | `GET /api/admin/relay/peerlink`, or `bvc relay peerlink` |
| `POST /api/relay/peer_redeem` | Removed |
| `peer_link` player permission | Removed. A peer declared in `config.hcl` is allowed to connect. |
| Certificates with the name `server::{host}:{port}` | The server refuses the connection. |

Link each pair of servers again. Run `bvc relay peerlink` on each server, and paste the printed `peers` block into the other server's `config.hcl`. See [peering](/wiki/reference/peering/).

The default capability is `carry_speakers` only. A peer gets `query_audio` and `serve_audio` only if you name them. An empty `capabilities` list gives the peer nothing.

If two peers cannot connect directly, set `server.peer_relay_url`.

:::note
`server.peer_relay_url` is removed after beta.21. After beta.21, peers must connect directly. There is no relay. See [peering](/wiki/reference/peering/).
:::

## Java mod

`embedded-config` now uses the same keys as the BVC server's own configuration. The flat keys are removed.

:::caution
The embedded server **does not start** while an old key is present. It logs each old key with its replacement and stops. The mod does not change the file.
:::

File: `plugins/BedrockVoiceChat/config.yml` (Paper), `config/bedrock-voice-chat.json` (Fabric)

| Old key | New key |
|---|---|
| `http-port` | `server.port` |
| `quic-port` | `server.quic_port` |
| `tls-certificate` | `server.tls.certificate` |
| `tls-key` | `server.tls.key` |
| `tls-names` | `server.tls.names` |
| `tls-ips` | `server.tls.ips` |
| `assets-path` | `server.assets_path` |
| `broadcast-range` | `voice.spatial_audio.broadcast_range` |
| `log-level` | `log.level` |
| `allow-audio-upload` | `permissions.defaults.audio_upload` |
| `allow-audio-delete` | `permissions.defaults.audio_delete` |

The camelCase spellings (`httpPort`, `tlsCertificate`, and the others) change in the same way.

The same configuration as nested blocks:

```yaml
use-embedded-server: true
embedded-config:
  server:
    port: 8444
    quic_port: 8443
    tls:
      certificate: "/path/to/fullchain.pem"
      key: "/path/to/privkey.pem"
      names:
        - "bvc.example.com"
  voice:
    spatial_audio:
      broadcast_range: 32.0
  log:
    level: "info"
```

A key that you do not set uses the server default. See the [Java mod](/wiki/server/java-mod/) pages.

## Bedrock Addon

Each entry in `server.bedrock.servers` must set `addon_mode`. It selects how position, state and chat events for the world reach the BVC server.

| Value | Use for |
|---|---|
| `net` | A world that runs the standard Bedrock Addon or the Java mod. The Addon or the mod sends events to the BVC server over HTTP. |
| `no_net` | A Realms or Aternos world that runs the [no-net Addon](/wiki/server/nonet-addon/). The BVC client reads the events from the game traffic and sends them. |

The `BVC_BEDROCK_SERVERS` environment variable accepts an optional last token, `@net` or `@no_net`:

```
Name@host[:port][@protocol][@net|@no_net]
```

The server identifies each of the last two tokens from its value: a number is the protocol, and `net` or `no_net` is the mode. You can omit either token and write them in either order. See [environment variables](/wiki/reference/environment-variables/#bedrock).

## Hytale

The Hytale Java mod is removed, with its build and release pipeline.
